<h1 id="picaso-internal-functions">PICASO Internal Functions</h1>
<div class="pdf-hide">
<div class="admonition note">

<h2 id="introduction">Introduction</h2>
<p>The 4D Labs family of embedded graphics processors are powered by a highly optimised soft-core virtual engine, E.V.E. (Extensible Virtual Engine). EVE was designed and created by 4D Labs in the early 2000’s and should not be confused by FTDI’s solution of EVE, which was developed a decent decade or so later.</p>
<p>EVE is a proprietary, high performance virtual processor with an extensive byte-code instruction set optimised to execute compiled 4DGL programs. 4DGL (4D Graphics Language) was specifically developed from ground up for the EVE engine core. It is a high-level language which is easy to learn and simple to understand yet powerful enough to tackle many embedded graphics applications.</p>
<p>4DGL is a graphics-oriented language allowing rapid application development. An extensive library of graphics, text and file system functions and the ease of use of a language that combines the best elements and syntax structure of languages such as C, Basic, Pascal, etc. Programmers familiar with these languages will feel right at home with 4DGL. It includes many familiar instructions such as <code>IF..ELSE..ENDIF, WHILE..WEND, REPEAT..UNTIL, GOSUB..ENDSUB, GOTO</code> as well as a wealth of (chip-resident) internal functions that include <code>SERIN, SEROUT, GFX_LINE, GFX_CIRCLE</code> and many more.</p>
<p>This document covers the internal (chip-resident) functions available for the PICASO Processor. This document should be used in conjunction with the <a href="../">4DGL Programmers Reference Manual</a>.</p>
<figure>
<p><img alt="PICASO Internal Block Diagram" class="pdf-only width-60" src="../img/picaso/image1.png"></p>
<figcaption>
<p><em>PICASO Internal Block Diagram</em></p>
</figcaption>
</figure>

<h2 id="c-type-functions">C Type Functions</h2>
<h3 id="isdigit">isdigit</h3>
<p>Tests the character parameter and returns a 1 if the character is an ASCII digit else returns a 0. Valid range: "0123456789".</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>isdigit(char);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">Specifies the ASCII character for the test.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>:   0 if character is not as ASCII digit, 1 if character is an ASCII digit.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="isxdigit">isxdigit</h3>
<p>Tests the character parameter and returns a 1 if the character is an ASCII hexadecimal digit else returns a 0.
Valid range: "0123456789ABCDEF".</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>isxdigit(char);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">Specifies the ASCII character for the test.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  0 if character is not as ASCII hexadecimal digit, 1 if character is an ASCII hexadecimal digit. </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:  Refer to <a href="#isdigit">isdigit Example</a></p>

<h3 id="disp_sync">disp_Sync</h3>
<p>Allows the program to synchronise writing to the hardware for flicker free operation. Some
experimentation may be needed to find an optimum line for <code>disp_Sync</code> depending on the graphics
operation. The higher the value, the slower the throughput. A certain point will be reached (number
of scanlines + blanking lines within the vertical retrace period) where it will just 'hang up' stopping
the entire process. Eg, in 640x480 mode, if the 'lines' value is 507, operation will be slowest (as its
actually right at the end of the blanking period) and 508 will cause a hangup situation as it is above
the highest scanline value.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>disp_Sync(line);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">line</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">Scan line.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  16-bit value in the register.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Applies to uVGA-II/III modules only.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="disp_disconnect">disp_Disconnect</h3>
<p>This function disconnects the display driver pins and/or reconfigures it to achieve its lowest possible power consumption. Use after disabling peripheral power to ensure the minimal power usage by the display.</p>
<!-- New in v3.8 PmmC -->

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>disp_Disconnect();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<!-- TODO: Add example -->

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p><a href="#disp_init">disp_Init()</a> should be used to reinitialise the display.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="disp_init">disp_Init</h3>
<p>This function is used to initialise the display.
This is useful in a number of situations, however mainly for the uLCD-xx-PTU modules which have the ability to disable the power supply to the display for low power sleep modes. This function is required to re-initialise the display once power to the display has been restored, so the display is usable once again.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>disp_Init();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<!-- TODO: Add example -->

<h3 id="file_count">file_Count</h3>
<p>Returns number of files found that match the criteria.
The wild card character '<strong>*</strong>' matches up with any combination of allowable characters and '<strong>?</strong>' matches up with any single allowable character.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Count(filename);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">filename</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Name of the file(s) for the search (passed as a string).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Number of files that match the criteria.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-11-1" name="__codelineno-11-1" href="#__codelineno-11-1"></a><span class="nl">count</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Count</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"*.4XE"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Returns number of files with “.4XE”.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_dir">file_Dir</h3>
<p>Streams a string of file names that agree with the search key. Returns number of files found that match the criteria. The wild card character '<strong>*</strong>' matches up with any combination of allowable characters and '<strong>?</strong>' matches up with any single allowable character.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Dir(filename);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">filename</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Name of the file(s) for the search (passed as a string).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Number of files that match the criteria.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-12-1" name="__codelineno-12-1" href="#__codelineno-12-1"></a><span class="nl">count</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Dir</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"*.4XE"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Returns number of files with “.4XE”.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_findfirst">file_FindFirst</h3>
<p>Returns true if at least 1 file exists that satisfies the file argument.
Wildcards are usually used so if <code>file_FindFirst</code> returns true, further tests can be made using <a href="#file_findnext">file_FindNext()</a>; to find all the files that match the wildcard class. Note that the stream behaviour is the same as <a href="#file_dir">file_Dir</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_FindFirst(fname);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Name of the file(s) for the search (passed as a string).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>:   1 If at least one file exists that satisfies the criteria. 0 If no file satisfies the criteria.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-13-1" name="__codelineno-13-1" href="#__codelineno-13-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">file_FindFirst</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"*.4XE"</span><span class="p">))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-13-2" name="__codelineno-13-2" href="#__codelineno-13-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"File Found"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-13-3" name="__codelineno-13-3" href="#__codelineno-13-3"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_findnext">file_FindNext</h3>
<p>Returns true if more file exists that satisfies the file argument that was given for <a href="#file_findfirst">file_FindFirst</a>. Wildcards must be used for <a href="#file_findfirst">file_FindFirst</a>, else this function will always return zero as the only occurrence will have already been found.
Note that the stream behaviour is the same as <a href="#file_dir">file_Dir</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_FindNext();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if more files exist that satisfy the criteria set in the <code>file_FindFirst(fname)</code>. 0 if no more files satisfy the criteria set in the <code>file_FindFirst(fname)</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-14-1" name="__codelineno-14-1" href="#__codelineno-14-1"></a><span class="k">while</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">((</span><span class="n">file_FindNext</span><span class="p">()))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-14-2" name="__codelineno-14-2" href="#__codelineno-14-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">filecount</span><span class="o">++</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-14-3" name="__codelineno-14-3" href="#__codelineno-14-3"></a><span class="n">wend</span>
</code></pre></div>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_open">file_Open</h3>
<p>Returns handle if file exists. The file "<strong>handle</strong>" that is created is now used as reference for "filename" for further file functions such as <a href="#file_close">file_Close(handle)</a>, etc. For <code>FILE_WRITE</code> and <code>FILE_APPEND</code> modes (<code>'w'</code> and <code>'a'</code>) the file is created if it does not exist.</p>
<p>If the file is opened for append, and it already exists, the file pointer is set to the end of the file ready for appending, else the file pointer will be set to the start of the newly created file.</p>
<p>If the file was opened successfully, the internal error number is set to 0 (i.e. no errors) and can be read with the <a href="#file_error">file_Error()</a> function.</p>
<p>For <code>FILE_READ</code> mode (<code>'r'</code>) the file must exist else a null handle (0) is returned and the 'file not found' error number is set which can be read with the <a href="#file_error">file_Error()</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Open(fname, mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Name of the file(s) for the search (passed as a string).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><code>FILE_READ</code> (<code>'r'</code>), <code>FILE_WRITE</code> (<code>'w'</code>) or <code>FILE_APPEND</code> (<code>'a'</code>)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Handle if file exists. Sets internal file error number accordingly (0 if no errors).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>If a file is opened for write mode 'w', and the file already exists, the operation will fail. Unlike C and some other languages where the file will be erased ready for re-writing when opened for writing, 4DGL offers a simple level of protection that ensures that a file must be purposely erased before being re-written.</li>
<li>Beginning with the v4.0 PmmC a file opened with FILE_APPEND may be randomly read and or written. Also any altered file will have the Archive bit set in the directory entry.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<h3 id="file_read">file_Read</h3>
<p>Reads the number of bytes specified by <strong>size</strong> from the file referenced by <strong>handle</strong> into a destination memory buffer.
Destination is always a word pointer, as you can only read into RAM which is word addressable.
If <strong>destination</strong> is zero, data is read direct to GRAM window.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Read(*destination, size, hanlde);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">destination</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination memory buffer. This is a normal word aligned address.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of bytes to be read</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file to be read.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Number of characters read.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-17-1" name="__codelineno-17-1" href="#__codelineno-17-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Read</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">memblock</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hndl1</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_seek">file_Seek</h3>
<p>Places the file pointer at the required position in a file that has been opened in <code>'r'</code> (read) or <code>'a'</code> (append) mode. In append mode, <code>file_Seek</code> does not expand a filesize, instead, the file pointer (handle) is set to the end position of the file, e.g.:- assuming the file size is 10000 bytes, <code>file_Seek(handle, 0, 0x1234);</code> will set the file position to 0x00001234 (byte position 4660) for the file handle, so subsequent data may be read from that position onwards with <a href="#file_getc">file_GetC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_getw">file_GetW(...)</a>, <a href="#file_gets">file_GetS(...)</a>, or an image can be displayed with <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...)</a>. Conversely, <a href="#file_putc">file_PutC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_putw">file_PutW(...)</a> and <a href="#file_puts">file_PutS(...)</a> can write to the file at the position. A <strong>FE_EOF</strong> (end of file error) will occur if you try to write or read past the end of the file.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Seek(handle, HiWord, LoWord);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">HiWord</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the upper 16bits of the memory pointer into the file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LoWord</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the lower 16bits of the memory pointer into the file</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  TRUE if ok, usually ignored.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-18-1" name="__codelineno-18-1" href="#__codelineno-18-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Seek</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hSource</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x0000</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x1234</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_index">file_Index</h3>
<p>Places the file pointer at the position in a file that has been opened in <code>'r'</code> (read) or <code>'a'</code> (append) mode. In append mode, <code>file_Index</code> does not expand a filesize, instead, the file pointer (handle) is set to the end position of the file, e.g.:- assuming the record size is 100 bytes, <code>file_Index(handle, 0, 100, 22);</code> will set the file position to 2200 for the file handle, so subsequent data may be read from that position onwards with <a href="#file_getc">file_GetC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_getw">file_GetW(...)</a>, <a href="#file_gets">file_GetS(...)</a>, or an image can be displayed with <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...)</a>. Conversely, <a href="#file_putc">file_PutC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_putw">file_PutW(...)</a> and <a href="#file_puts">file_PutS(...)</a> can write to the file at the position. A <strong>FE_EOF</strong> (end of file error) will occur if you try to write or read past the end of the file.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Index(handle, Hisize, LoSize, recordnum);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Hisize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the upper 16bits of the size of the file records.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LoSize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the lower 16bits of the size of the file records.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">recordnum</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The index of the required record.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  TRUE if ok, usually ignored.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:  </p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-19-1" name="__codelineno-19-1" href="#__codelineno-19-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Index</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hSource</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">22</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>

<h3 id="file_screencapture">file_ScreenCapture</h3>
<p>Save an image of the screenshot to file at the current file position.</p>
<p>The image can later be displayed with <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...);</a>. The file may be opened in append mode to accumulate multiple images. Later, the images can be displayed with <a href="#file_seek">file_Seek(...)</a>.</p>
<p>The image is saved from x, y (with respect to top left corner), and the capture area is determined by "width" and "height".</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_ScreenCapture(x, y, width, height, handle);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<td style="text-align: center;">x</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">X-position of the image to be captured.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Y-position of the image to be captured.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">width</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Width of the area to be captured.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">height</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Height of the area to be captured.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file to store the image(s).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: Zero (0) if function successful.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="file_putc">file_PutC</h3>
<p>This function writes the byte specified by "char" to the file, at the position indicated by the associated file-position pointer and advances the pointer appropriately (incremented by 1). The file must be previously opened with <code>'w'</code> (write) or <code>'a'</code> (append) modes.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_PutC(char, handle);</code></p>

<h3 id="file_puts">file_PutS</h3>

<h3 id="file_gets">file_GetS</h3>
<p>This function reads a line of text to a buffer (specified by "<strong>*string</strong>") from a file at the current file position indicated by the associated file-position pointer and advances the pointer appropriately.</p>
<p><strong>file_GetS(...)</strong> will stop reading when any of the following conditions are true:</p>
<p>a. It has read n-1 bytes (one character is reserved for the null-terminator)
b. It encounters a newline character (a line-feed in the compilers tested here)
c. It reaches the end of file
d. A read error occurs.</p>
<p>The file must be previously opened with <code>'r'</code> (read) mode.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_GetS(*string, size, handle);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">string</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination buffer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The maximum number of bytes to be read from the file.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The number of characters read from file (excluding the null terminator)</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-30-1" name="__codelineno-30-1" href="#__codelineno-30-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_GetS</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mystring</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">80</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="file_loadfunction">file_LoadFunction</h3>
<p>Load a function or program from disk and return a function pointer to the allocation.</p>
<p>The function can then be invoked just like any other function would be called via a function pointer. Parameters may be passed to it in a conventional way. The function may be discarded at any time when no longer required, thus freeing its memory resources.</p>
<p>The loaded function can be discarded with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(..)</a> Note that any pointer references passed to the child function may not include references to the parents DATA statements or any static string references. Any string or array information must be in the parents global or local memory space. The reason for this is that DATA statements and static strings are contained in the parents CODE segment, and cannot be accessed by the child process.</p>
<p>The callers stack is shared by the loaded function, however any global variables in the loaded function are private to that function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_LoadFunction(fname.4XE);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname.4XE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Name of the 4DGL application program that is about to be loaded into RAM.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the memory allocation where the function has been loaded from file which can be then used as a function call.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>PmmC Rev 31 and above has an added feature where a parent can access the child global Variables when using <code>file_LoadFunction(fname.4XE)</code>.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="file_run">file_Run</h3>
<p>Any memory allocations in the main FLASH program are released, however, the stack and globals are maintained.</p>
<p>If <strong>arglistptr</strong> is 0, no arguments are passed, else <strong>arglistptr</strong> points to an array, the first element containing the number of additional elements in the array which contain the arguments.</p>
<p>func 'main' in the called program accepts the arguments, if any.</p>
<p>The disk does not need to be mounted, <code>file_Run</code> automatically mounts the drive.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Run(fname.4XE, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname.4XE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">name of the 4DGL child program to be loaded into RAM and executed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value from main in the called program.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-35-45" name="__codelineno-35-45" href="#__codelineno-35-45"></a><span class="cm">/*===================================================================</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-46" name="__codelineno-35-46" href="#__codelineno-35-46"></a><span class="cm">Redraw the button matrix. Only draw buttons that have changed state.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-47" name="__codelineno-35-47" href="#__codelineno-35-47"></a><span class="cm">The top lef corner of the button matrix is set with the xorg and yorg parameters depending on the font and text string width, the button matrix dynamically resizes.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-48" name="__codelineno-35-48" href="#__codelineno-35-48"></a><span class="cm">Parameters:-</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-49" name="__codelineno-35-49" href="#__codelineno-35-49"></a><span class="cm">maxwidth    = rhs from xorg (in pixels) to cause wrap at rhs</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-50" name="__codelineno-35-50" href="#__codelineno-35-50"></a><span class="cm">maxwidth    = maximum matrix width (in pixel units)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-51" name="__codelineno-35-51" href="#__codelineno-35-51"></a><span class="cm">buttoncount = number of buttons to display</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-52" name="__codelineno-35-52" href="#__codelineno-35-52"></a><span class="cm">font        = FONT1 to FONT4</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-53" name="__codelineno-35-53" href="#__codelineno-35-53"></a><span class="cm">xorg:yorg   = top left corner of button array</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-54" name="__codelineno-35-54" href="#__codelineno-35-54"></a><span class="cm">NB:- The  touch detect matrix array is updated when any button changes state.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-55" name="__codelineno-35-55" href="#__codelineno-35-55"></a><span class="cm">When you need to draw the matrix for the first instance of the matrix, you must</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-56" name="__codelineno-35-56" href="#__codelineno-35-56"></a><span class="cm">call with mode = 1 to instantiate the buttons.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-57" name="__codelineno-35-57" href="#__codelineno-35-57"></a><span class="cm">call with mode = 0 for normal button action.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-35-58" name="__codelineno-35-58" href="#__codelineno-35-58"></a><span class="cm">===================================================================*/</span>

<h3 id="file_exec">file_Exec</h3>
<p>This function is similar to <a href="#file_run">file_Run</a>, however, the main program in FLASH retains all memory allocations (e.g. file buffers, memory allocated with <a href="#mem_alloc">mem_Alloc</a> etc).</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Exec(fname.4XE, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Name of the 4DGL child program to be loaded into RAM and executed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program or 0 if no arguments.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value from main in the called program.</p>

<div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--prev" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div><div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--next" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div></div>
<h3 id="file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl</h3>
<p>Reads a control file to create an image list.</p>
<p id="file_loadimagecontrol_modes">The following are the modes of operation</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Mode</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">It is assumed that there is a graphics file with the file extension "fname2.gci". In this case, the images have been stored in a FAT16 file concurrently, and the offsets that are derived from the "fname1.dat" file are saved in the image control so that the image control can open the file (<em>.gci) and use <a href="#file_seek">file_Seek(...)</a> to get to the position of the image which can then automatically be displayed using <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...)</a>. Mode 0 builds the image control quickly as it only scans the </em>.dat file for the file offsets and saves them in the relevant entries in the image control. The penalty is that images take longer to find when displayed due to <a href="#file_seek">file_Seek(...)</a> overheads.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">It is assumed that there is a graphics file with the file extension "fname2.gci". In this case, the images have been stored in a FAT16 file concurrently, and the offset of the images are saved in the image control so that image file (*.gci) can be mapped to directly. The absolute cluster/sector is mapped so file seek does not need to be called internally. This means that there is no seek time penalty, however, the image list takes a lot longer to build, as all the seeking is done at control build time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">In this case, the images have been stored in a in a RAW partition of the uSD card, and the absolute address of the images are saved in the DAT file. This is the fastest operation of the image control as there is no seeking or other disk activity taking place.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>When an image control is loaded, an array is built in RAM. It consists of a 6 word header with the following entries as defined by the constants:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Information</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Index</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">IMG_COUNT</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">IMG_ENTRYLEN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">IMG_MODE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">IMG_GCI_FILENAME</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">IMG_DAT_FILENAME</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">4</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">IMG_GCIFILE_HANDLE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>No images are stored in FLASH or RAM, the image control holds the index values for the absolute storage positions on the uSD card for RAW mode, or the cluster/sector position for formatted FAT16 mode.</p>
<p>When an image control is no longer required, the memory can be released with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free()</a>;</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_LoadImageControl(fname1, fname2, mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The control list filename "*.dat". Created from Graphics Composer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The image filename "*.gci". Created from Graphics Composer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Determines the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol_modes">mode of operation</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<!-- TODO: Confirm if 'fname1' and 'fname2' accept string (byte-aligned) pointer or array (word-aligned) pointer -->

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Pointer (handle) to the memory allocation to the image control list that has been created, null (0) if function fails</p>

<h3 id="file_mount">file_Mount</h3>
<p>Starts up the FAT16 disk file services and allocates a small 32 byte control block for subsequent use. When you open a file using <a href="#file_open">file_Open(...)</a>, a further 512 + 44 = 556 bytes are attached to the FAT16 file control block. When you close a file using <a href="#file_close">file_Close(...)</a>, the 556 byte allocation is released leaving the 32 byte file control block. The <code>file_Mount()</code> function must be called before any other FAT16 file related functions can be used. The control block and all FAT16 file resources are completely released with <a href="#file_unmount">file_Unmount()</a>. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_Mount();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: True (1) if successful, False (0) otherwise</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-39-1" name="__codelineno-39-1" href="#__codelineno-39-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">!</span><span class="n">file_Mount</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-39-2" name="__codelineno-39-2" href="#__codelineno-39-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">repeat</span>
<a id="__codelineno-39-3" name="__codelineno-39-3" href="#__codelineno-39-3"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Disk not mounted"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-39-4" name="__codelineno-39-4" href="#__codelineno-39-4"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-39-5" name="__codelineno-39-5" href="#__codelineno-39-5"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">gfx_Cls</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-39-6" name="__codelineno-39-6" href="#__codelineno-39-6"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-39-7" name="__codelineno-39-7" href="#__codelineno-39-7"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">until</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Mount</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-39-8" name="__codelineno-39-8" href="#__codelineno-39-8"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_unmount">file_Unmount</h3>
<p>Release any buffers for FAT16 and unmount the Disk File System. This function is to be called to close the FAT16 file system.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_Unmount();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-40-1" name="__codelineno-40-1" href="#__codelineno-40-1"></a><span class="n">file_Unmount</span><span class="p">();</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_playwav">file_PlayWAV</h3>
<p>Open the wav file, decode the header to set the appropriate wave player parameters and set off the playing of the file as a background process. See <a href="#sound-control-functions">Sound Control Functions</a> for additional play control functions.</p>
<p id="file_playwav_err_codes">This function may return the following values if unsuccessful:</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Error Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-7</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Insufficient memory available for WAV buffer and file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-6</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">cant play this rate</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no data chunk found in first rsector</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no format data</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no wave chunk signature</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">bad wave file format</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">file not found</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_PlayWAV(fname);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filename of the wav file to be opened and played</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Number of blocks to play (1 to 32767), or <a href="#file_playwav_err_codes">error code</a> otherwise.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-41-1" name="__codelineno-41-1" href="#__codelineno-41-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">ding.wav</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">);</span>

<a id="__codelineno-41-3" name="__codelineno-41-3" href="#__codelineno-41-3"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">pitch</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">NOTES</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="p">];</span>

<h2 id="flash-memory-functions">Flash Memory Functions</h2>
<p>The functions in this section only apply to serial SPI (NAND) flash devices interfaced to the Picaso SPI port.</p>
<h3 id="flash_sig">flash_SIG</h3>
<p>If a FLASH storage device is connected to the SPI port, and has been correctly initialised with the
<a href="#spi_init">spi_Init(...)</a> function, the Electronic Signature of the device can be read using this function. The only
devices supported so far on the Picaso are the M25Pxx range of devices which are 512Kbit to 32Mbit
(2M x 8) Serial Flash Memory.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_SIG();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Release from Deep Power-down, and Read Electronic Signature. Only the low order
byte is valid, the upper byte is ignored.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-42-1" name="__codelineno-42-1" href="#__codelineno-42-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">sig</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">id</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-42-2" name="__codelineno-42-2" href="#__codelineno-42-2"></a><span class="n">spi_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI_SLOW</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RXMODE_0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">CKMODE_0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-42-3" name="__codelineno-42-3" href="#__codelineno-42-3"></a><span class="c1">//...</span>
<a id="__codelineno-42-4" name="__codelineno-42-4" href="#__codelineno-42-4"></a><span class="nl">sig</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">flash_SIG</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-42-5" name="__codelineno-42-5" href="#__codelineno-42-5"></a><span class="nl">id</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">flash_ID</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-42-6" name="__codelineno-42-6" href="#__codelineno-42-6"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Flash Signature:"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">HEX4</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">sig</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-42-7" name="__codelineno-42-7" href="#__codelineno-42-7"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Flash (JEDEC)ID:"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">HEX4</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">id</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="flash_id">flash_ID</h3>
<p>If a FLASH storage device is connected to the SPI port, and has been correctly initialised with the
<a href="#spi_init">spi_Init(...)</a> function, the memory type and capacity from the flash device can be read using this
function. The only devices supported so far on the Picaso are the M25Pxx range of devices which are
512Kbit to 32Mbit (2M x 8) Serial Flash Memory.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_ID();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Reads the memory type and capacity from the serial FLASH device. Hi byte contains
type, and low byte contains capacity. Refer to the device data sheet for further information.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<p>Refer to the example under the <a href="#flash_sig">flash_SIG()</a> section.</p>
<h3 id="flash_bulkerase">flash_BulkErase</h3>
<p>If a FLASH storage device is connected to the SPI port, and has been correctly initialised with the
<a href="#spi_init">spi_Init(...)</a> function, the FLASH device can be completely erased using this function. The only devices
supported so far on the Picaso are the M25Pxx range of devices which are 512Kbit to 32Mbit (2M x 8) Serial Flash Memory.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_BulkErase();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Erases the entire flash media device. The function returns no value, and the operation can take up to
80 seconds depending on the size of the flash device.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="flash_blockerase">flash_BlockErase</h3>
<p>If a FLASH storage device is connected to the SPI port, and has been correctly initialised with the
<a href="#spi_init">spi_Init(...)</a> function, the FLASH block can be erased using this function. The only devices supported
so far on the Picaso are the M25Pxx range of devices which are 512Kbit to 32Mbit (2M x 8) Serial Flash Memory.
E.g. there are 32 x 64K blocks on a 2Mb flash device.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_BlockErase(blockAddress);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">blockAddress</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The address of the 64k FLASH block to be erased.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Erases the required block in a FLASH media device. The function returns no value, and the operation can take up to 3 milliseconds.</p>
</div>

<h3 id="lookup8">lookup8</h3>
<p>Search a list of 8-bit constant values for a match with a search value <strong>key</strong>. If found, the index of the matching constant is returned in <strong>result</strong>, else <strong>result</strong> is set to zero. Thus, if the value is found first in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to one. If second in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to two etc. If not found, <strong>result</strong> is returned with zero.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>lookup8(key, byteConstList);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">key</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A byte value to search for in a fixed list of constants. The <strong>key</strong> argument can be a variable, array element, expression or constant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">byteConstList</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A comma separated list of constants and strings to be matched against <strong>key</strong>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The index of the matching constant, otherwise zero.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-44-1" name="__codelineno-44-1" href="#__codelineno-44-1"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>

<a id="__codelineno-44-9" name="__codelineno-44-9" href="#__codelineno-44-9"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">lookup8</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">key</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x4D</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"abcd"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'Z'</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span>

</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The list of constants cannot be re-directed. The <code>lookup8(...)</code> function offer a versatile way for returning an index for a given value. This can be very useful for data entry filtering and parameter input checking and where ever you need to check the validity of certain inputs. The entire search list field can be replaced with a single name if you use the $ operator in constant, e.g. :</p>
<p><code>#constant HEXVALUES $"0123456789ABCDEF"</code></p>
</div>
<h3 id="lookup16">lookup16</h3>
<p>Search a list of 16-bit constant values for a match with a search value <strong>key</strong>. If found, the index of the matching constant is returned in <strong>result</strong>, else <strong>result</strong> is set to zero. Thus, if the value is found first in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to one. If second in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to two etc. If not found, <strong>result</strong> is returned with zero.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<td style="text-align: center;">key</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A byte value to search for in a fixed list of constants. The <strong>key</strong> argument can be a variable, array element, expression or constant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">wordConstList</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A comma separated list of constants to be matched against <strong>key</strong>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The index of the matching constant, otherwise zero</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-45-10" name="__codelineno-45-10" href="#__codelineno-45-10"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="k">else</span>
<a id="__codelineno-45-11" name="__codelineno-45-11" href="#__codelineno-45-11"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">Value not found"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-45-12" name="__codelineno-45-12" href="#__codelineno-45-12"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">endif</span>
<a id="__codelineno-45-13" name="__codelineno-45-13" href="#__codelineno-45-13"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">Ok"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// all done</span>
<a id="__codelineno-45-14" name="__codelineno-45-14" href="#__codelineno-45-14"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">repeat</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">forever</span>
<a id="__codelineno-45-15" name="__codelineno-45-15" href="#__codelineno-45-15"></a><span class="n">endfunc</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The <code>lookup16(...)</code> function offer a versatile way for returning an index for a given value. This is very useful for parameter input checking and where ever you need to check the validity of certain values. The entire search list field can be replaced with a single name by using the $ operator in constant, e.g.:</p>
<p><code>#constant LEGALVALS $5,10,20,50,100,200,500,1000,2000,5000,10000</code></p>
</div>

<h3 id="pin_hi">pin_HI</h3>
<p>Outputs a "High" level (logic 1) on the appropriate pin that was previously selected as an Output. 
If the pin is not already set to an output, it is automatically made an output.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>pin_HI(pin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the pin number .</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-47-1" name="__codelineno-47-1" href="#__codelineno-47-1"></a><span class="n">pin_HI</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO2_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// output a Logic 1 on IO2 pin</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="pin_lo">pin_LO</h3>
<p>Outputs a "Low" level (logic 0) on the appropriate pin that was previously selected as an Output. 
If the pin is not already set to an output, it is automatically made an output.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>pin_LO(pin);</code></p>

<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-48-1" name="__codelineno-48-1" href="#__codelineno-48-1"></a><span class="n">pin_LO</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// output a Logic 0 on IO1 pin</span>

<h3 id="pin_read">pin_Read</h3>
<p>Reads the logic state of the pin that was previously selected as an Input. Returns a "Low" (logic 0) or "High" (logic 1).</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>pin_Read(pin);</code></p>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A Logic 1 (0x0001) or a Logic 0 (0x0000) or the analogue value of the input pin.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-49-1" name="__codelineno-49-1" href="#__codelineno-49-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">pin_Read</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">==</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// read the value on IO1</span>
<a id="__codelineno-49-2" name="__codelineno-49-2" href="#__codelineno-49-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">calc_Threshold</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-49-3" name="__codelineno-49-3" href="#__codelineno-49-3"></a><span class="k">else</span>
<a id="__codelineno-49-4" name="__codelineno-49-4" href="#__codelineno-49-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="p">...</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="bus_in">bus_In</h3>
<p>Returns the state of the bus as an 8bit value in to the lower byte of the assigned variable.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The BUS_RD and BUS_WR pins are not affected.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>bus_In();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The state of the bus as a 8bit value.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-50-1" name="__codelineno-50-1" href="#__codelineno-50-1"></a><span class="nl">var1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">bus_In</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-50-2" name="__codelineno-50-2" href="#__codelineno-50-2"></a><span class="c1">// The lower byte of var1 will get loaded with the state of the bus.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="bus_out">bus_Out</h3>
<p>The lower byte of the argument is placed on the 8bit wide bus. The upper byte of the argument is ignored.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The BUS_RD and BUS_WR pins are not affected. Any BUS pins that are set to inputs are not affected.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>bus_Out(arg1);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arg</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the pin number.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-51-1" name="__codelineno-51-1" href="#__codelineno-51-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">temp</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-51-2" name="__codelineno-51-2" href="#__codelineno-51-2"></a><span class="nl">temp</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x0015</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-51-3" name="__codelineno-51-3" href="#__codelineno-51-3"></a><span class="n">bus_Out</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">temp</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Set the Bus output</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="bus_set">bus_Set</h3>
<p>The lower 8 bits of arg1 are placed in the BUS direction register. </p>
<p>A '1' sets a pin to be an input, a '0' sets a pin to be output.</p>
<p>The upper 8 bits of arg1 are ignored. The BUS_RD and BUS_WR pins are not affected.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>bus_Set(arg1);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arg</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the pin number.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-52-1" name="__codelineno-52-1" href="#__codelineno-52-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">arg1</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-52-2" name="__codelineno-52-2" href="#__codelineno-52-2"></a><span class="nl">arg1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xAA</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//</span>
<a id="__codelineno-52-3" name="__codelineno-52-3" href="#__codelineno-52-3"></a><span class="n">bus_Set</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">arg1</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Set the bus to value specified to arg1</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="bus_read">bus_Read</h3>
<p>Returns the state of the bus as a 8bit value in to the lower byte of the assigned variable.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The BUS_RD and BUS_WR pins are not affected. The BUS_RD pin set to LO, then, after a settling
delay of approx 50nsec, the BUS is read into the lower 8 bits of the assigned variable (the upper 8 bits
being set to 0) the BUS_RD pin is then set back to a HI level.
The BUS_RD pin is automatically pre-set to an output to ensure BUS write integrity.</p>
</div>
<p><img alt="bus_Read" src="../img/picaso/image2.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>bus_Read();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The state of the bus as a 8bit value.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-53-1" name="__codelineno-53-1" href="#__codelineno-53-1"></a><span class="nl">var1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">bus_Read</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-53-2" name="__codelineno-53-2" href="#__codelineno-53-2"></a><span class="c1">// The lower byte of var1 will get loaded with the state of the bus.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="bus_write">bus_Write</h3>
<p>The lower 8 bits of arg1 are placed on the BUS, then, after a settling delay of approx 50nsec, the
BUS_WR pin is strobed LO for approx 50nsec then set back HI. The upper 8 bits of arg1 are ignored.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The BUS_WR pin is automatically pre-set to an output to ensure BUS write integrity.</p>
</div>
<p><img alt="bus_Write" src="../img/picaso/image3.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>bus_Write(data);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">data</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The lower 8-bits of <strong>data</strong> are sent to the bus.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-54-1" name="__codelineno-54-1" href="#__codelineno-54-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">data1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-54-2" name="__codelineno-54-2" href="#__codelineno-54-2"></a><span class="nl">data1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x05</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-54-3" name="__codelineno-54-3" href="#__codelineno-54-3"></a><span class="n">bus_Write</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">data1</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="graphics-functions">Graphics Functions</h2>
<h3 id="gfx_cls">gfx_Cls</h3>
<p>Clear the screen using the current background colour. <strong>gfx_Cls()</strong> command brings some of the settings back to default; such as,</p>
<ul>
<li>Transparency turned OFF</li>
<li>Outline colour set to BLACK</li>
<li>Opacity set to OPAQUE</li>
<li>Pen set to OUTLINE</li>
<li>Line patterns set to OFF</li>
<li>Right text margin set to full width</li>
<li>Text magnifications set to 1</li>
<li>All origins set to 0:0</li>
</ul>
<p>The alternative to maintain settings and clear screen is to draw a filled rectangle with the required background colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Cls();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-55-1" name="__codelineno-55-1" href="#__codelineno-55-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_BGcolour</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">DARKGRAY</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-55-2" name="__codelineno-55-2" href="#__codelineno-55-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Cls</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-55-3" name="__codelineno-55-3" href="#__codelineno-55-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-55-4" name="__codelineno-55-4" href="#__codelineno-55-4"></a><span class="c1">// This example clears the entire display using colour DARKGRAY</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="gfx_changecolour">gfx_ChangeColour</h3>
<p>Changes all <strong>oldColour</strong> pixels to <strong>newColour</strong> within the clipping area.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_ChangeColour(oldColour, newColour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">oldColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the sample colour to be changed within the clipping window.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">newColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the new colour to change all occurrences of old colour within the clipping window.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-56-1" name="__codelineno-56-1" href="#__codelineno-56-1"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>
<a id="__codelineno-56-2" name="__codelineno-56-2" href="#__codelineno-56-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">txt_Width</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 id="gfx_circle">gfx_Circle</h3>
<p>Draws a circle with centre point x1, y1 with radius r using the specified colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Circle(x, y, rad, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x,y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the centre of the circle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">rad</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the radius of the circle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the circle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-57-1" name="__codelineno-57-1" href="#__codelineno-57-1"></a><span class="c1">// assuming PEN_SIZE is OUTLINE</span>
<a id="__codelineno-57-2" name="__codelineno-57-2" href="#__codelineno-57-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Circle</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RED</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-57-3" name="__codelineno-57-3" href="#__codelineno-57-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-57-4" name="__codelineno-57-4" href="#__codelineno-57-4"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a BLUE circle outline centred at x=50, y=50 with a radius of 30 pixel units.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The default <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, however, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>SOLID</strong>, the circle will be drawn filled, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, the circle will be drawn as an outline. If the circle is drawn as SOLID, the outline colour can be specified with <a href="#gfx_outlinecolour">gfx_OutlineColour(...)</a>. If <strong>OUTLINE_COLOUR</strong> is set to 0, no outline is drawn.</p>
</div>

<h3 id="gfx_polyline">gfx_Polyline</h3>
<p>Plots lines between points specified by a pair of arrays using the specified colour. The lines may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function. gfx_Polyline can be used to create complex raster graphics by loading the arrays from serial input or from MEDIA with very little code requirement.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Polyline(n, vx, vy, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">n</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of elements in the x and y arrays specifying the vertices for the polyline.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vx</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the x coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vy</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the y coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the lines.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-64-1" name="__codelineno-64-1" href="#__codelineno-64-1"></a><span class="cp">#inherit "4DGL_16bitColours.fnc"</span>

<a id="__codelineno-64-5" name="__codelineno-64-5" href="#__codelineno-64-5"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>

<a id="__codelineno-64-50" name="__codelineno-64-50" href="#__codelineno-64-50"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a simple scene</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="gfx_polygon">gfx_Polygon</h3>
<p>Plots lines between points specified by a pair of arrays using the specified colour. The last point is drawn back to the first point, completing the polygon. The lines may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function. gfx_Polygon can be used to create complex raster graphics by loading the arrays from serial input or from MEDIA with very little code requirement.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Polygon(n, vx, vy, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">n</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of elements in the x and y arrays specifying the vertices for the polygon.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vx</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the x coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vy</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the y coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the polygon.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-65-1" name="__codelineno-65-1" href="#__codelineno-65-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">vx</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">7</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">vy</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">7</span><span class="p">];</span>
<a id="__codelineno-65-2" name="__codelineno-65-2" href="#__codelineno-65-2"></a>

<h3 id="gfx_triangle">gfx_Triangle</h3>
<p>Draws a triangle outline between vertices x1,y1 , x2,y2 and x3,y3 using the specified colour. The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function. Vertices must be specified in an anti-clockwise fashion.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Triangle(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the first vertices of the triangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the second vertices of the triangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x3, y3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the third vertices of the triangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the triangle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-66-1" name="__codelineno-66-1" href="#__codelineno-66-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_Triangle</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">CYAN</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-66-2" name="__codelineno-66-2" href="#__codelineno-66-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-66-3" name="__codelineno-66-3" href="#__codelineno-66-3"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a CYAN triangular outline with vertices at 10,10 30,10 20,30</span>
</code></pre></div>
