<h3 id="gfx_bullet">gfx_Bullet</h3>
<p>Draws a <strong>circle</strong> or 'bullet point' with radius <strong><em>r</em></strong> at the current origin using the current object colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Bullet(radius);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">radius</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the radius of the bullet.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-68-1" name="__codelineno-68-1" href="#__codelineno-68-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-68-2" name="__codelineno-68-2" href="#__codelineno-68-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Bullet</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// Draw a 10pixel radius Bullet at x=30, y=30.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The default <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, however, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>SOLID</strong>, the circle will be drawn filled, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, the circle will be drawn as an outline. If the circle is drawn as <strong>SOLID</strong>, the outline colour can be specified with <a href="#gfx_outlinecolour">gfx_OutlineColour(...)</a>.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit</h3>
<p>Sets up the internal pointers for the <a href="#gfx_orbit">gfx_Orbit(..)</a> result variables. The &amp;<strong>x_orb</strong> and &amp;<strong>y_orb</strong> parameters are the addresses of the variables or array elements that are used to store the result from the <a href="#gfx_orbit">gfx_Orbit(..)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_OrbitInit(&amp;x_dest, &amp;y_dest);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x_dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage locations for the calculated Orbit X-coordinate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y_dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage locations for the calculated Orbit Y-coordinate.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-69-1" name="__codelineno-69-1" href="#__codelineno-69-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-69-2" name="__codelineno-69-2" href="#__codelineno-69-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_OrbitInit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-69-3" name="__codelineno-69-3" href="#__codelineno-69-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-69-4" name="__codelineno-69-4" href="#__codelineno-69-4"></a><span class="c1">// This example sets the variables that will receive the result from a gfx_Orbit(..) function call</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="gfx_orbit">gfx_Orbit</h3>
<p>Sets Prior to using this function, the destination address of variables for the calculated coordinates must be set using the <a href="#gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit(..)</a> function. The <strong>gfx_Orbit(..)</strong> function calculates the x, y coordinates of a distant point relative to the current origin, where the only known parameters are the <strong>angle</strong> and the <strong>distance</strong> from the current origin. The new coordinates are calculated and then placed in the destination variables that have been previously set with the <a href="#gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit(..)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Orbit(angle, distance);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">angle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the angle from the origin to the remote point. The angle is specified in degrees.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">distance</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the distance from the origin to the remote point in pixel units.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-70-1" name="__codelineno-70-1" href="#__codelineno-70-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-70-2" name="__codelineno-70-2" href="#__codelineno-70-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-70-3" name="__codelineno-70-3" href="#__codelineno-70-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_OrbitInit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-70-4" name="__codelineno-70-4" href="#__codelineno-70-4"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-70-5" name="__codelineno-70-5" href="#__codelineno-70-5"></a><span class="n">gfx_Bullet</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">                                   </span><span class="c1">// mark the start point with a small WHITE circle</span>
<a id="__codelineno-70-6" name="__codelineno-70-6" href="#__codelineno-70-6"></a><span class="n">gfx_Orbit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                              </span><span class="c1">// calculate a point 50 pixels away from origin at</span>
<a id="__codelineno-70-7" name="__codelineno-70-7" href="#__codelineno-70-7"></a><span class="w">                                                </span><span class="c1">// 30 degrees</span>
<a id="__codelineno-70-8" name="__codelineno-70-8" href="#__codelineno-70-8"></a><span class="n">gfx_CircleFilled</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mh">0xF800</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// mark the target point</span>
<a id="__codelineno-70-9" name="__codelineno-70-9" href="#__codelineno-70-9"></a><span class="w">                                                </span><span class="c1">// with a RED circle</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>See example comments for explanation.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Result is stored in the variables that were specified with the <a href="#gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit(..)</a> function.</p>

<h3 id="gfx_moverel">gfx_MoveRel</h3>
<p>Moves the origin to a new position relative to the old position.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_MoveRel(xoffset, yoffset);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xoffset</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal offset of the new origin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">yiffset</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the vertical offset of the new origin.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>

<h3 id="gfx_incx">gfx_IncX</h3>
<p>Increment the current X origin by 1 pixel unit. The original value is returned before incrementing. The return value can be useful if a function requires the current point before insetting occurs.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_IncX();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The current X origin before the increment.</p>

<h3 id="gfx_lineto">gfx_LineTo</h3>
<p>Draws a line from the current origin to a new position. The Origin is then set to the new position. The line is drawn using the current object colour. The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_LineTo(xpos, ypos);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xpos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal position of the line end as well as the new origin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ypos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the vertical position of the line end as well as the new origin.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-77-1" name="__codelineno-77-1" href="#__codelineno-77-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-77-2" name="__codelineno-77-2" href="#__codelineno-77-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_LineTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">60</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">70</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-77-3" name="__codelineno-77-3" href="#__codelineno-77-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-77-4" name="__codelineno-77-4" href="#__codelineno-77-4"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a line using the current object colour between x1=10,y1=20 and x2=60,y2=70. The new origin is now set at x=60,y=70.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="gfx_linerel">gfx_LineRel</h3>
<p>Draws a line from the current origin to a new position. The line is drawn using the current object colour. The current origin is not altered. The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_LineRel(xpos, ypos);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xpos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal end point of the line.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ypos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the vertical end point of the line.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-78-1" name="__codelineno-78-1" href="#__codelineno-78-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_LinePattern</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mb">0b1100110011001100</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-78-2" name="__codelineno-78-2" href="#__codelineno-78-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-78-3" name="__codelineno-78-3" href="#__codelineno-78-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_LineRel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-78-4" name="__codelineno-78-4" href="#__codelineno-78-4"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-78-5" name="__codelineno-78-5" href="#__codelineno-78-5"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a tessellated line using the current object colour between 10,20 and 50,50.</span>

<h3 id="gfx_boxto">gfx_BoxTo</h3>
<p>Draws a rectangle from the current origin to the new point using the current object colour. The top left corner is anchored by the current origin (x1, y1), the bottom right corner is specified by x2, y2.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_BoxTo(x2, y2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the diagonally opposed corner of the rectangle to be drawn, the top left corner (assumed to be x1, y1) is anchored by the current origin.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="gfx_button">gfx_Button</h3>
<p>Draws a 3-dimensional Text Button at screen location defined by x, y parameters (top left corner). The size of the button depends on the font, width, height and length of the text. The button can contain multiple lines of text by having the <code>\n</code> character embedded in the string for the end of line marker. In this case, the widest text in the string sets the overall width, and the height of the button is set by the number of text lines. In the case of multiple lines, each line is left justified. If you wish to centre or right justify the text, you will need to prepare the text string according to your requirements.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Button(state, x, y, buttonColour, txtColour, font, txtWidth, txtHeight, text);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">state</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 = Button pressed; 1 = Button raised.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner position of the button on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buttonColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Button colour.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">txtColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Text Colour.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">font</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the Font ID.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">txtWidth</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the width of the text. This value is the font width multiplier and minimum value must be 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">txtHeight</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the height of the text. This value is the font height multiplier and minimum value must be 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">text</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the text string. The text string must be within the range of printable ascii character set. The string may have <code>\n</code> characters embedded to create a multiline button.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>

<h3 id="gfx_slider">gfx_Slider</h3>
<p>Draws a vertical or horizontal slider bar on the screen. The gfx_Slider function has several different
modes of operation. In order to minimise the amount of graphics functions we need, all modes of
operation are selected naturally depending on the parameter values.</p>
<p>Selection rules:</p>
<ol>
<li>If x2-x1 &gt; y2-y1 slider is assumed to be horizontal (i.e. if width &gt; height, slider is horizontal).</li>
<li>If x2-x1 &lt;= y2-y1 slider is assumed to be vertical (i.e. if height &lt;= width, slider is horizontal).</li>
<li>If value is positive, thumb is set to the position that is the proportion of value to the scale parameter.(used to set the control to the actual value of a variable)</li>
<li>If value is negative, thumb is driven to the graphics position set by the ABSolute of value. (used to set thumb to its actual graphical position (usually by touch screen)</li>
<li>The thumb colour is determine by <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Set(OBJECT_COLOUR, value);</a>, however, if the current object colour is BLACK, a darkened shade of the colour parameter is used for the thumb.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Slider2(mode, x1, y1, x2, y2, colour, scale, value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">mode = 0 : Slider Indented, mode = 1 : Slider Raised, mode 2, Slider Hidden (background colour).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner position of the slider on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the bottom right corner position of the slider on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the Slider bar.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">scale</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Scale = n : sets the full scale range of the slider for the thumb from 0 to n.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">If value positive, sets the relative position of the thumb on the slider bar, else set thumb to ABS position of the negative number.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  If the value parameter was a positive number (i.e. value is a proportion of the scale parameter), the true (implied x-axis or y-axis) position of the thumb is returned. <br>
If the value parameter was a negative number (i.e. thumb is being set to an ABSolute graphics position), the actual slider value (which is a proportion of the scale parameter) is returned.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-84-1" name="__codelineno-84-1" href="#__codelineno-84-1"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">drawRedSlider</span><span class="p">()</span>

<h3 id="gfx_screencopypaste">gfx_ScreenCopyPaste</h3>
<p>Copies an area of a screen from xs, ys of size given by width and height parameters and pastes it to another location determined by xd, yd.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_ScreenCopyPaste(xs, ys, xd, yd, width, height);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xs, ys</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the top left corner of the area to be copied (source).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xd, yd</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the top left corner of where the paste is to be made (destination).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">width</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the width of the copied area.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">height</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the height of the copied area.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-85-1" name="__codelineno-85-1" href="#__codelineno-85-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_ScreenCopyPaste</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">40</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">40</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 id="gfx_polygonfilled">gfx_PolygonFilled</h3>
<p>Draws a solid Polygon between specified vertices: <em>x1,y1</em>, <em>x2,y2</em> ... <em>xn,yn</em> using the specified colour. The last point is drawn back to the first point, completing the polygon. Vertices must be minimum of 3 and can be specified in any fashion.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_PolygonFilled(n, vx, vy, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">n</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of elements in the x and y arrays specifying the vertices for the polygon.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vx</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the x coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vy</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the y coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the polygon.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>

<tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">Get current internal Y position</td>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the maximum horizontal value of the display.</td>

<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the maximum vertical value of the display.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the left location of the last drawn object such as a slider or button or an image/video.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the top location of the last drawn object such as a slider or button or an image/video.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the right location of the last drawn object such as a slider or button or an image/video.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the bottom location of the last drawn object such as a slider or button or an image/video.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">6</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the internal X position that was set with <a href="#gfx_moveto">gfx_MoveTo(x, y)</a>; or <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Set(X_ORG, pos)</a>;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">7</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the internal Y position that was set with <a href="#gfx_moveto">gfx_MoveTo(x, y)</a>; or <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Set(X_ORG, pos)</a>;</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 id="gfx_clipwindow">gfx_ClipWindow</h3>
<p>Specifies a clipping window region on the screen such that any objects and text placed onto the screen will be clipped and displayed only within that region. For the clipping window to take effect, "Clipping" setting must be enabled separately using <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Set(CLIPPING, ON)</a> or the shortcut <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Clipping(ON)</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_ClipWindow(x1, y1, x2, y2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the top left corner of the clipping window.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the bottom right corner of the clipping window.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h2 id="i2c-master-functions">I2C Master Functions</h2>
<h3 id="i2c_open">I2C_Open</h3>
<p>Calling this function configures the I2C module and initialises it to be ready for service. The I2C clock speed is specified by the <strong>speed</strong> parameter. Three I2C Speed settings are available to suit various requirements.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Constant</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Speed</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_SLOW</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">100KHz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_MED</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">400KHz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_FAST</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1MHz</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C_Open(Speed);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Speed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the I2C bus speed. (See the table above).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="i2c_start">I2C_Start</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C start condition.
The hardware first pulls the SDA (data) line low, and next pulls the SCL (clock) line low.</p>
<p><img alt="I2C_Start" src="../img/picaso/image4.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C_Start();</code></p>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="i2c_stop">I2C_Stop</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C stop condition. The hardware first releases the SCL to high state, and then releases the SDA line high.</p>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C_Stop();</code></p>

</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="i2c_ack">I2C_Ack</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C acknowledge condition. The hardware first pulls the SDA line low, and next releases SCL high followed by pulling SCL low again thus generating a clock pulse, SDA is then released high.</p>
<p><img alt="i2c_ack" src="../img/picaso/image8.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C_Ack();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-100-1" name="__codelineno-100-1" href="#__codelineno-100-1"></a><span class="n">I2C_Ack</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Send I2C Acknowledge condition</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Data can only change when the clock is low.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="i2c_nack">I2C_Nack</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C negative acknowledge condition. The hardware first release the SDA line high, and next releases SCL HI followed by pulling SCL low thus generating a clock pulse.</p>
<p><img alt="i2c_nak" src="../img/picaso/image9.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C_Nack();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-101-1" name="__codelineno-101-1" href="#__codelineno-101-1"></a><span class="n">I2C_Nack</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//Send an I2C Negative acknowledge condition</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Data can only change when the clock is low.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="i2c_ackstatus">I2C_AckStatus</h3>
<p>Call this function to get the ACK status from the slave device
The state of SDA is returned.</p>
<p><img alt="i2c_ackstatus" src="../img/picaso/image10.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C_AckStatus();</code></p>

<h2 id="image-control-functions">Image Control Functions</h2>
<h3 id="img_setposition">img_SetPosition</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a>; function.</p>
<p>Sets the position where the image will next be displayed. Returns TRUE if index was ok and function was successful. (the return value is usually ignored).</p>
<p>You may turn off an image so when <a href="#img_show">img_Show()</a> is called, the image will not be shown.</p>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a>; function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_SetPosition(handle, index, xpos, ypos);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the Image List.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the images in the list.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xpos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Top left horizontal screen position where image is to be displayed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ypos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Top left vertical screen position where image is to be displayed.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True if index OK, otherwise false.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-109-1" name="__codelineno-109-1" href="#__codelineno-109-1"></a><span class="c1">// make a simple 'window'</span>
<a id="__codelineno-109-2" name="__codelineno-109-2" href="#__codelineno-109-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Panel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">PANEL_RAISED</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">239</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">239</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">GRAY</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-109-3" name="__codelineno-109-3" href="#__codelineno-109-3"></a><span class="n">img_SetPosition</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Ihndl</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BTN_EXIT</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">224</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">            </span><span class="c1">//set checkout box position</span>
<a id="__codelineno-109-4" name="__codelineno-109-4" href="#__codelineno-109-4"></a><span class="n">img_Enable</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Ihndl</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BTN_EXIT</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                        </span><span class="c1">//enable checkout box</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="img_enable">img_Enable</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...);</a> function.</p>
<p>Enables a selected image in the image list. Returns TRUE if index was ok and function was successful. This is the default state so when <a href="#img_show">img_Show()</a> is called all the images in the list will be shown.</p>
<p>To enable all the images in the list at the same time set index to -1.</p>
<p>To enable a selected image, use the image index number.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_Enable(handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the Image List.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the images in the list.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True if index OK, otherwise False.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-110-1" name="__codelineno-110-1" href="#__codelineno-110-1"></a><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">img_Enable</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hImageList</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">imagenum</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="img_disable">img_Disable</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...);</a> function.</p>
<p>Disables an image in the image list. Returns TRUE if index was ok and function was successful. Use this function to turn off an image so that when <a href="#img_show">img_Show()</a> is called the selected image in the list will not be shown.</p>
<p>To disable all the images in the list at the same time set index to -1.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_Disable(handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the Image List.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the images in the list.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True if index OK, otherwise False.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-111-1" name="__codelineno-111-1" href="#__codelineno-111-1"></a><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">img_Disable</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hImageList</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">imagenum</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="img_darken">img_Darken</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...);</a> function.</p>
<p>Darken an image in the image list. Returns TRUE if index was ok and function was successful. Use this function to darken an image so that when <a href="#img_show">img_Show()</a> is called the control will take effect. To darken all the images in the list at the same time set index to -1.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_Darken(handle, index);</code></p>

<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the images in the list.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True if index OK, otherwise False.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="img_setattributes">img_SetAttributes</h3>
<p>This function SETS one or more bits in the IMAGE_FLAGS field of an image control entry. 
"value" refers to various bits in the image control entry (see image attribute flags).</p>
<p>A '1' bit in the "value" field SETS the respective bit in the IMAGE_FLAGS field of the image control entry.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Flag Constant</th>

<tbody>

<td style="text-align: left;">Set for image enabled.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_DARKEN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">14</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x4000</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Display dimmed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_LIGHTEN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">13</td>

<td style="text-align: left;">Display bright.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_TOUCHED</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">12</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x1000</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Touch test result.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_Y_LOCK</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">11</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0800</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Stop Y movement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_X_LOCK</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">10</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0400</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Stop X movement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_TOPMOST</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">9</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0200</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_STAYONTOP</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">8</td>

</tr>

<h3 id="img_clearattributes">img_ClearAttributes</h3>
<p>Clear various image attribute flags in an image control entry. (see image attribute flags below)</p>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> function.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>

<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the Image List.</td>

<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the images in the list.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">a '1' bit indicates that a bit should be set and a '0' bit indicates that a bit is not altered.</td>

</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If index is set to -1, the attribute is altered in ALL of the entries in the image list. 
The constant ALL is set to -1 specifically for this purpose.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: Returns TRUE if if index was ok and function was successful, usually ignored </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-118-1" name="__codelineno-118-1" href="#__codelineno-118-1"></a><span class="n">img_ClearAttributes</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">value</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Image attribute flags may be combined with the + or | operators,
e.g.:- img_ClearAttributes(hndl, ALL, I_Y_LOCK | I_X_LOCK ); // allow all images to move in any direction.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="img_touched">img_Touched</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> function.</p>
<p>Returns index if image touched or returns -1 image not touched.
If index is passed as -1 the function tests all images and returns -1 if image not touched or returns index.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_Touched(handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

</thead>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the images in the list.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  <strong>index</strong> of image touched, released or being held, or <strong>-1</strong> if none</p>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">A variable, array element, expression or constant.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The absolute value.</p>

<h3 id="sin">SIN</h3>
<p>This function returns the SIN of an <strong>angle</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>SIN(angle);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">angle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The angle in degrees.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The input value is automatically shifted to lie within 0-359 degrees.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The sine in radians of an argument specified in degrees. The returned value range is from 127 to -127 which is a more useful representation for graphics work. The real sine values vary from 1.0 to -1.0 so appropriate scaling must be done in user code as required.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-124-1" name="__codelineno-124-1" href="#__codelineno-124-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">angle</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-124-2" name="__codelineno-124-2" href="#__codelineno-124-2"></a><span class="nl">angle</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">133</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-124-3" name="__codelineno-124-3" href="#__codelineno-124-3"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">SIN</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">angle</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-124-4" name="__codelineno-124-4" href="#__codelineno-124-4"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-124-5" name="__codelineno-124-5" href="#__codelineno-124-5"></a><span class="c1">// This example returns 92 in variable myvar.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="cos">COS</h3>
<p>This function returns the COSINE of an <strong>angle</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>COS(angle);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">angle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The angle in degrees.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The input value is automatically shifted to lie within 0-359 degrees.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The cosine in radians of an argument specified in degrees. The returned value range is from 127 to -127 which is a more useful representation for graphics work. The real sine values vary from 1.0 to -1.0 so appropriate scaling must be done in user code as required.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="rand">RAND</h3>
<p>This function returns a pseudo random signed number ranging from -32768 to +32767.</p>
<p>The random number generator may first be seeded by using the SEED(number) function. The seed will generate a pseudo random sequence that is repeatable. You can use the modulo operator (%) to return a number within a certain range, e.g. n := RAND() % 100; will return a random number between -99 and +99. If you are using random number generation for random graphics points, or only require a positive number set, you will need to use the ABS function so only a positive number is returned, e.g.: X1 := ABS(RAND() % 100); will set co-ordinate X1 between 0 and 99.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>RAND();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pseudo random signed number ranging from -32768 to +32767 each time the function is called.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-126-1" name="__codelineno-126-1" href="#__codelineno-126-1"></a><span class="n">SEED</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1234</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-126-2" name="__codelineno-126-2" href="#__codelineno-126-2"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">(),</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">", "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">());</span>
<a id="__codelineno-126-3" name="__codelineno-126-3" href="#__codelineno-126-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-126-4" name="__codelineno-126-4" href="#__codelineno-126-4"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print 3558, 1960 to the display.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If the random number generator is not seeded, the first number returned after reset or power up will be zero. This is normal behavior.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="seed">SEED</h3>
<p>This function seeds the pseudo random number generator so it will generate a new repeatable sequence. The seed value can be a positive or negative number.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>SEED(number);</code></p>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-127-1" name="__codelineno-127-1" href="#__codelineno-127-1"></a><span class="n">SEED</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">-50</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 id="ovf">OVF</h3>
<p>This function returns the high order 16-bits from certain math and shift functions. 
It is extremely useful for calculating 32-bit address offsets for MEDIA access.</p>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>OVF();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The high order 16-bits from certain math and shift functions.</p>

<h3 id="umul_1616">umul_1616</h3>
<p>Performs an unsigned multiply of 2 x 16bit values placing the 32bit result in a 2 word array.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>umul_1616(&amp;res32, val1, val2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;res32</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to 32bit result register.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">val1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">16bit register or constant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">val2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">16bit register or constant.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the 32bit result. Carry and overflow are not affected.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-133-3" name="__codelineno-133-3" href="#__codelineno-133-3"></a><span class="n">umul_1616</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">val32</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">500</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2000</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-133-4" name="__codelineno-133-4" href="#__codelineno-133-4"></a><span class="nl">p</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str_Ptr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">val32</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 id="ucmp_3232">ucmp_3232</h3>
<p>Performs an unsigned comparison of 2 x 32bit values.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>ucmp_3232(&amp;val1, &amp;val2);</code></p>

</tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">Points to 32bit variable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">Points to 32bit variable.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h2 id="media-functions">Media Functions</h2>
<h3 id="media_init">media_Init</h3>
<p>Initialise a uSD/SD/SDHC memory card for further operations. The SD card is connected to the SPI (serial peripheral interface) of the Picaso chip.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Init();</code>  </p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if memory card is present and successfully initialised. 0 if no card is present or not able to initialise.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="media_setadd">media_SetAdd</h3>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LOword</td>

</tbody>

<h3 id="media_readword">media_ReadWord</h3>
<p>Returns the word value (2 bytes) from the current media address. The internal byte address will then be internally incremented by two. If the address is not aligned, the word will still be read correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_ReadWord();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Returns the word value (2 bytes) from the current media address.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-141-5" name="__codelineno-141-5" href="#__codelineno-141-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">myword</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">media_ReadWord</span><span class="p">();</span>

<a id="__codelineno-141-7" name="__codelineno-141-7" href="#__codelineno-141-7"></a><span class="n">endif</span>

</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Writing bytes or words to a media sector must start from the beginning of the sector. All writes will be incremental until the <a href="#media_flush">media_Flush()</a> function is executed, or the sector address rolls over to the next sector. When <a href="#media_flush">media_Flush()</a> is called, any remaining bytes in the sector will be padded with 0xFF, destroying the previous contents. An attempt to use the <a href="#media_setadd">media_SetAdd(..)</a> function will result in the lower 9 bits being interpreted as zero. If the writing rolls over to the next sector, the <a href="#media_flush">media_Flush()</a> function is issued automatically internally.</p>
</div>

<h3 id="media_flush">media_Flush</h3>
<p>After writing any data to a sector, <a href="#media_flush">media_Flush()</a> should be called to ensure that the current sector that is being written is correctly stored back to the media else write operations may be unpredictable.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Flush();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Non-zero if OK, 0 if Failed.  </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See the <a href="#media_writebyte">media_WriteByte(..)</a> and <a href="#media_writeword">media_WriteWord(..)</a> examples.</p>
<h3 id="media_image">media_Image</h3>

If the image is shown partially off-screen, it may not be displayed correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Image(x, y);</code></p>

<h3 id="media_video">media_Video</h3>
<p>Displays a video clip from the media storage device at the specified co-ordinates. The video address location in the media is previously specified with the <a href="#media_setadd">media_SetAdd(..)</a> or <a href="#media_setsector">media_SetSector(...)</a> function. If the video is shown partially off-screen, it may not be displayed correctly. Note that showing a video blocks all other processes until the video has finished showing. See the <a href="#media_videoframe">media_VideoFrame(...)</a> functions for alternatives.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Video(x, y);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left position where the video clip will be displayed.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-145-1" name="__codelineno-145-1" href="#__codelineno-145-1"></a><span class="k">while</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">media_Init</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="o">==</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">             </span><span class="c1">// wait if no SD card detected</span>

<h3 id="media_videoframe">media_VideoFrame</h3>
<p>Displays a video from the media storage device at the specified co-ordinates. The video address is previously specified with the <a href="#media_setadd">media_SetAdd(..)</a> or <a href="#media_setsector">media_SetSector(...)</a> function. If the video is shown partially off it may not be displayed correctly. The frames can be shown in any order. This function gives you great flexibility for showing various icons from an image strip, as well as showing videos while doing other tasks.</p>
<p><a href="#media_videoframe">media_VideoFrame(..)</a> will now show error box for out of range video frames. Also, if frame is set to -1, just a rectangle will be drawn in background colour to blank an image. It applies to PmmC R29 or above.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_VideoFrame(x, y, frameNumber);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left position where the video clip will be displayed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">frameNumber</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the required frame to be shown.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h2 id="memory-allocation-functions">Memory Allocation Functions</h2>
<h3 id="mem_alloc">mem_alloc</h3>
<p>Allocate a block of memory to pointer myvar. The allocated memory contains garbage but is a fast allocation.</p>
<p>The block must later be released with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(myvar);</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Alloc(size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes that's allocated from the heap.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Value is the pointer (Word) to the allocation if successful. If function fails returns a null (0).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-148-1" name="__codelineno-148-1" href="#__codelineno-148-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Alloc</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_allocv">mem_AllocV</h3>
<p>Allocate a block of memory to pointer myvar. The block of memory is filled with initial signature values.</p>
<p>The block starts with A5,5A then fills with incrementing number e.g.:- A5,5A,00,01,02,03...FF,00,11....</p>
<p>This can be helpful when debugging. The block must later be released with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(myvar)</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_AllocV(size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes that's allocated from the heap.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Value is the pointer (Word) to the allocation if successful. If function fails returns a null (0).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-149-1" name="__codelineno-149-1" href="#__codelineno-149-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_AllocV</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_allocz">mem_AllocZ</h3>
<p>Allocate a block of memory to pointer myvar. The block of memory is filled with zeros.</p>
<p>The block must later be released with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(myvar);</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_AllocZ(size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes that's allocated from the heap.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Value is the pointer to the allocation if successful. If function fails returns a null (0).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-150-1" name="__codelineno-150-1" href="#__codelineno-150-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_AllocZ</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_realloc">mem_Realloc</h3>
<p>The function may move the memory block to a new location, in which case the pointer to the new location is returned.</p>
<p>The content of the memory block is preserved up to the least of the new and old sizes, even if the block is moved.</p>
<p>If the new size is larger, the value of the newly allocated portion is indeterminate.</p>
<p>In case that ptr is NULL, the function behaves exactly as <a href="#mem_alloc">mem_Alloc()</a>, assigning a new block of size bytes and returning a pointer to the beginning of it.</p>
<p>In case that the size is 0, the memory previously allocated in ptr is deallocated as if a call to <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(myvar)</a> was made, and a NULL pointer is returned.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Realloc(ptr, size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the new location to reallocate the memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes of the block.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Pointer to the new object location.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-151-1" name="__codelineno-151-1" href="#__codelineno-151-1"></a><span class="nl">newptr</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Realloc</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myptr</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_free">mem_free</h3>
<p>The function de-allocates a block of memory previously created with <a href="#mem_alloc">mem_Alloc(...)</a>, <a href="#mem_allocv">mem_AllocV(...)</a> or <a href="#mem_allocz">mem_AllocZ(...)</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Free(allocation);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">allocation</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the location of memory block to free up.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Non-zero if function is successful, 0 if the function fails.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-152-1" name="__codelineno-152-1" href="#__codelineno-152-1"></a><span class="nl">test</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Free</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_heap">mem_Heap</h3>
<p>Returns byte size of the largest chunk of memory available in the heap.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Heap();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The largest available byte memory chunk in the heap.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-153-1" name="__codelineno-153-1" href="#__codelineno-153-1"></a><span class="nl">howmuch</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Heap</span><span class="p">();</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="mem_copy">mem_Copy</h3>
<p>Copy a word aligned block of memory from source to destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Copy(source, destination, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">source</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the source memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">destination</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the destination memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the size of the blocks in bytes.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Source.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-155-1" name="__codelineno-155-1" href="#__codelineno-155-1"></a><span class="nl">myptr</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Copy</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ptr1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">ptr2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The count is a byte count, this facilitates comparing word aligned byte arrays when using word aligned packed strings.
Source can be a string constant e.g. 
``` cpp
myptr := mem_Copy("TEST STRING", ptr2, 12);
````</p>
</div>
<h3 id="mem_compare">mem_Compare</h3>
<p>Compare two blocks of memory <strong>ptr1</strong> and <strong>ptr2</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Compare(ptr1, ptr2, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the 1st memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the 2nd memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes to compare.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  </p>
<ul>
<li>0 if we have a match</li>
<li>-1 if ptr1 &lt; ptr2</li>
<li>+1 if ptr2 &gt; ptr1. (The comparison is done alphabetically)</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-156-1" name="__codelineno-156-1" href="#__codelineno-156-1"></a><span class="nl">test</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Compare</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">this_block</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">that_block</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="serial-uart-functions">Serial (UART) Functions</h2>

<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-157-1" name="__codelineno-157-1" href="#__codelineno-157-1"></a><span class="n">setbaud</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BAUD_19200</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// To set Com0 to 19200 BAUD rate.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Baud rates each have degree of accuracy for several reasons. The actual baud rate you would receive and relevant error% compared to the setting value, can be calculated.</p>
<p>ActualBaud is calculated using the following formula: <code>ActualBaud = 2812500/(trunc(2812500/RequiredBaud))</code></p>
<p>Example for 115200 is, 2812500/115200 = 24.414, Trucated is 24. 2812500/37 = 117188 (rounded). <br>
Error% therefore is % difference between 115200 and 117188, therefore 1.73%</p>
<p>It is desirable to only use a baud rate between 2 devices which has a difference of typically &lt; 2%.
Note both devices will have a degree of error, not just this 4D Processor, both need to be
considered.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="com_setbaud">com_SetBaud</h3>
<p>Use this function to set the required baud rate for the required Com port.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_SetBaud(“comport”, “baudrate/10”);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">comport</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the Com port, COM0 or COM1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">baudrate/10</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the baud rate.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True if BAUD rate was acceptable.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-158-1" name="__codelineno-158-1" href="#__codelineno-158-1"></a><span class="nl">stat</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">com_SetBaud</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">COM1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">9600</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">        </span><span class="c1">// To set Com1 to 9600 BAUD rate.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-158-2" name="__codelineno-158-2" href="#__codelineno-158-2"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">stat</span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-158-3" name="__codelineno-158-3" href="#__codelineno-158-3"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="err">“</span><span class="n">Com1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">set</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">to</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">9600</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BAUD</span><span class="err">”</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-158-4" name="__codelineno-158-4" href="#__codelineno-158-4"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Baud Rates are not always precise, and an approximate error can be seen from the <a href="#setbaud">setbaud()</a>
functions table on the previous page.</p>
<p>Baud rates each have degree of accuracy for several reasons. The actual baud rate you would receive and relevant error% compared to the setting value, can be calculated.</p>
<p>ActualBaud is calculated using the following formula: <code>ActualBaud = 2812500/(trunc(2812500/RequiredBaud))</code></p>
<p>Example for 115200 is, 2812500/115200 = 24.414, Trucated is 24. 2812500/37 = 117188 (rounded). <br>
Error% therefore is % difference between 115200 and 117188, therefore 1.73%</p>
<p>It is desirable to only use a baud rate between 2 devices which has a difference of typically &lt; 2%.
Note both devices will have a degree of error, not just this 4D Processor, both need to be
considered.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="serin">serin</h3>
<p><strong>serin():</strong> Receives a character from the Serial Port COM0.<br>
<strong>serin1():</strong> Receives a character from the Serial Port COM1.</p>
<p>serin may be buffered (refer to <a href="#com_init">com_Init(..)</a> functions). If it is desired to be able to receive the BREAK signal using buffered functions then the <a href="#com_initbrk">com_InitBrk()</a> function must be used instead.</p>
<p>The transmission format is: <strong>No Parity, 1 Stop Bit, 8 Data Bits</strong> (N,8,1). <br>
The default Baud Rate for COM0 is 115,200 bits per second or 115,200 baud. <br>
The default Baud Rate for COM1 is 9600 bits per second or 9600 baud.</p>
<p>The baud rate can be changed under program control by using the <a href="#setbaud">setbaud(...)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>serin();</code> or <code>serin1();</code>  </p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A positive value 0 to 255 for a valid character received.<br>-1 if no character is available. <br>-2 if a framing error or over-run has occurred (auto cleared). <br>-3 (BREAK) if a break signal is detected. </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-159-1" name="__codelineno-159-1" href="#__codelineno-159-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-159-2" name="__codelineno-159-2" href="#__codelineno-159-2"></a><span class="nl">char</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">serin</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">//test the com 0 port</span>
<a id="__codelineno-159-3" name="__codelineno-159-3" href="#__codelineno-159-3"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&gt;=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="c1">// if a valid character is received</span>
<a id="__codelineno-159-4" name="__codelineno-159-4" href="#__codelineno-159-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">process</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// process the character</span>
<a id="__codelineno-159-5" name="__codelineno-159-5" href="#__codelineno-159-5"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>

The default Baud Rate for COM0 is 115,200 bits per second or 115,200 baud. <br>
