<h3 id="com_init">com_Init</h3>
<p>This is the initialisation function for the serial communications buffered service. Once initialised, the service runs in the background capturing and buffering serial data without the user application having to constantly poll the serial port. This frees up the application to service other tasks.</p>
<p><strong>MODES OF OPERATION</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>No qualifier – simple ring buffer (aka circular queue)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p>If the <strong>qualifier</strong> is set to zero, the <strong>buffer</strong> is continually active as a simple circular queue. Characters when received from the host are placed in the circular queue (at the 'head' of the queue) Bytes may be removed from the circular queue (from the 'tail' of the queue) using the <a href="#serin">serin()</a> function. If the tail is the same position as the head, there are no bytes in the queue, therefore <a href="#serin">serin()</a> will return <strong>-1</strong>, meaning no character is available, also, the <a href="#com_count">com_Count()</a> function can be read at any time to determine the number of characters that are waiting between the tail and head of the queue. If the queue is not read frequently by the application, and characters are still being sent by the host, the head will eventually catch up with the tail setting the internal <code>COM_FULL</code> flag (which can be read with the <a href="#com_full">com_Full()</a> function) . Any further characters from the host are now discarded, however, all the characters that were buffered up to this point are readable. This is a good way of reading a fixed size packet and not necessarily considered to be an error condition. If no characters are removed from the buffer until the COM_FULL flag (which can be read with the <a href="#com_full">com_Full()</a> function) becomes set, it is guaranteed that the bytes will be ordered in the <strong>buffer</strong> from the start position, therefore, the <strong>buffer</strong> can be treated as an array and can be read directly without using serin() at all. In the latter case, the correct action is to process the data from the buffer, re-initialise the buffer with the <a href="#com_init">com_Init(..)</a> function, or reset the buffered serial service by issuing the <a href="#com_reset">com_Reset()</a> function (which will return serial reception to polled mode) , and send an acknowledgement to the host (traditionally a <strong>ACK</strong> or 6) to indicate that the application is ready to receive more data and the previous 'packet' has been dealt with, or conversely, the application may send a negative acknowledgement to indicate that some sort of error occurred, or the action could not be completed (traditionally a <strong>NAK</strong> or 16) .</p>
<p>If any low level errors occur during the buffering service (such as framing or over-run) the internal COM_ERROR flag will be set (which can be read with the <a href="#com_error">com_Error()</a> function). Note that the COM_FULL flag will remain latched to indicate that the buffer did become full, and is not reset (even if all the characters are read) until the <a href="#com_init">com_Init(..)</a> or <a href="#com_reset">com_Reset()</a> function is issued.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Using a qualifier</strong></li>
</ul>
<p>If a <strong>qualifier</strong> character is specified, after the buffer is initialised with <a href="#com_initt">com_Init(..)</a> , the service will ignore all characters until the <strong>qualifier</strong> is received and only then initiate the buffer write sequence with incoming data. After that point, the behaviour is the same as above for the 'non-qualified' mode.</p>
<p><strong>com_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier):</strong> Initialize a serial capture buffer for COM0.<br>
<strong>com1_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier):</strong> Initialize a serial capture buffer for COM1.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code> or <code>com1_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buffer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the address of a buffer used for the background buffering service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the byte size of the user array provided for the buffer (each array element holds 2 bytes). If the buffer size is zero, a buffer of 128 words (256 bytes) should be provided for automatic packet length mode (see below).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">qualifier</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the qualifying character that must be received to initiate serial data reception and buffer write. A zero (0x00) indicates no qualifier to be used.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-161-1" name="__codelineno-161-1" href="#__codelineno-161-1"></a><span class="n">com_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">combuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="c1">//set up a comms ring buffer for COM0, 20 characters before overflow</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="com_full">com_Full</h3>
<p>If the queue is not read frequently by the application, and characters are still being sent by the host, the head will eventually catch up with the tail setting the COM_FULL flag which is read with this function. <h3 id="com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer</h3>
<p>Initialise a serial buffer for the <strong>COM0</strong> or <strong>COM1</strong> output. </p>
<p>The program must declare a var array as a circular buffer. When a TX buffer is declared for comms, the transmission of characters becomes non-blocking.
The only time blocking will occur is if the buffer has insufficient space to accept the next character, in which case the function will wait for buffer space
to become available. If the TX buffer is no longer required, just set the buffer pointer to zero, the size in this case doesn't matter and is ignored. The function can resize or reallocated to another buffer at any time. The buffer is flushed before any changes are made.</p>
<p>"pin" designates an IO pin to control a bidirectional control device for half duplex mode. "pin" will go HI at the start of a transmission, and will return low after the final byte is transmitted.</p>
<p>Once the buffer has been initialised you just continue to use <a href="#serout">serout()</a> in the usual way, no other programming changes are required.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXbuffer(buf, bufsize, pin);</code> or <code>com1_TXbuffer(buf, bufsize, pin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the address of a buffer used for the buffering service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the byte size of the user array provided for the buffer (each array element holds 2 bytes).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the turnaround pin. If not required, just set "pin" to zero.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-167-1" name="__codelineno-167-1" href="#__codelineno-167-1"></a><span class="n">com_TXbuffer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1024</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// set the TX buffer</span>
<a id="__codelineno-167-2" name="__codelineno-167-2" href="#__codelineno-167-2"></a><span class="n">com_TXbuffer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="c1">// revert to non buffered service</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_txbufferhold">com_TXbufferHold</h3>
<p>This function is used in conjunction with <a href="#com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer(...)</a>.</p>
<p>It is often necessary to hold off sending serial characters until a complete frame or packet has been built in the output buffer. <strong>com_TXbufferHold(ON)</strong> is used for this, to stop the buffer being sent while it is being loaded. Normally, when using buffered comms, the transmit process will begin immediately. This is fine unless you are trying to assemble a packet.</p>
<p>To build a packet and send it later, issue a <strong>com_TXbufferHold(ON);</strong> build the packet, when packet is ready, issuing <strong>com_TXbufferHold(OFF);</strong>, will release the buffer to the com port.</p>
<p>Also, if using <a href="#com_txemptyevent">com_TXemptyEvent</a>, erroneous empty events will occur as the transmit buffer is constantly trying to empty while you are busy trying to fill it.</p>
<p>Also refer to the pin control for <a href="#com_txbufferr">com_TXbuffer(..)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXbufferHold(state);</code> or <code>com1_TXbufferHold(state);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">state</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the state of the buffer used for the buffering service.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  </p>
<ul>
<li>Buffer count when called with argument of 1, for example <strong>com_TXbufferHold(ON)</strong></li>
<li>0 when argument is zero, e.g. <strong>com_TXbufferHold(OFF)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: Refer to the <a href="#com_txemptyevent">com_TXemptyEvent(functionAddress)</a> example.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If you fill the buffer whilst it is held comms error 4 will be set and the data written will be lost.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="com_txcount">com_TXcount</h3>
<p>Return count of characters remaining in <strong>COM0</strong> or <strong>COM1</strong> transmit buffer that was previously allocated with <a href="#com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer(..);</a> or <strong>com1_TXbuffer(..);</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXcount();</code> or <code>com1_TXcount();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Count of characters.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-168-1" name="__codelineno-168-1" href="#__codelineno-168-1"></a><span class="nl">arg</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">com1_TXCount</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">          </span><span class="c1">//return count of characters in COM1 TX buffer</span>

<h3 id="com_txemptyevent">com_TXemptyEvent</h3>
<p>If a comms TX buffer that was previously allocated with <a href="#com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer(..)</a> or <strong>com1_TXbuffer(..)</strong>. This function can be used to set up a function to be called when the <strong>COM0</strong> or <strong>COM1</strong> TX buffer is empty.</p>
<p>This is useful for either reloading the TX buffer, setting or clearing a pin to change the direction of e.g. a RS485 line driver, or any other form of traffic control. The event function must not have any parameters. To disable the event, simply call <strong>com_TXemptyEvent(0)</strong> or <strong>com1_TXemptyEvent(0)</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="#com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer(..)</a> or <strong>com1_TXbuffer(..)</strong> also resets any active event.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXemptyEvent(functionAddress);</code> or <code>com1_TXemptyEvent(functionAddress);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">functionAddress</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Address of the event Function to be queued when COM0 or COM1 TX buffer empty.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Any previous event function address or zero if there was no previous function.</p>

<h2 id="sound-control-functions">Sound Control Functions</h2>
<h3 id="snd_volume">snd_Volume</h3>
<p>Set the sound playback volume. Var must be in the range from 8 (min volume) to 127 (max volume). If var is less than 8, volume is set to 8, and if var &gt; 127 it is set to 127.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_Volume(var);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">var</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">sound playback volume.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-170-1" name="__codelineno-170-1" href="#__codelineno-170-1"></a><span class="n">snd_Volume</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">127</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Set Volume to maximum</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="snd_pitch">snd_Pitch</h3>
<p>Sets the samples playback rate to a different frequency. Setting pitch to zero restores the original sample rate.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_Pitch(pitch)</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pitch</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sample's playback rate. Minimum is 4KHz. Range is, 4000 – 65535.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Sample's original sample rate.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-171-1" name="__codelineno-171-1" href="#__codelineno-171-1"></a><span class="n">snd_Pitch</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">7000</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//Play the wav file with a sample frequency of 7KHz.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="snd_bufsize">snd_BufSize</h3>
<p>Specify the memory chunk size for the wavefile buffer, default size 1024 bytes. Depending on the sample size, memory constraints, and the sample quality, it may be beneficial to change the buffer size from the default size of 1024 bytes.</p>
<p>This function is for control of a wav buffer, see the <a href="#file_playwav">file_PlayWAV(..)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_BufSize(var);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">var</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the buffer size. <br>0 = 1024 bytes (default) <br>1 = 2048 bytes <br>2 = 4096 bytes <br>3 = 8192 bytes</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-172-1" name="__codelineno-172-1" href="#__codelineno-172-1"></a><span class="n">snd_BufSize</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="c1">// allocate a 2048 byte wav buffer</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="snd_stop">snd_Stop</h3>
<p>Stop any sound that is currently playing, releasing buffers and closing any open wav file.
This function is for control of a wav buffer, see the <a href="#file_playwav">file_PlayWAV(..)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_Stop();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-173-1" name="__codelineno-173-1" href="#__codelineno-173-1"></a><span class="n">snd_Stop</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Stop, release buffers and close wav file</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="snd_pause">snd_Pause</h3>
<p>Pause any sound that is currently playing, does nothing until sound is resumed with <a href="#snd_continue">snd_Continue()</a>.</p>
<p>This function is for control of a wav buffer, see the <a href="#file_playwav">file_PlayWAV(..)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_Pause();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-174-1" name="__codelineno-174-1" href="#__codelineno-174-1"></a><span class="n">snd_Pause</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Pause Sound</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="snd_continue">snd_Continue</h3>
<p>Resume any sound that is currently paused by <a href="#snd_pause">snd_Pause</a>.</p>
<p>This function is for control of a wav buffer, see the <a href="#file_playwav">file_PlayWAV(..)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_Continue();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-175-1" name="__codelineno-175-1" href="#__codelineno-175-1"></a><span class="n">snd_Continue</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Continue sound</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="snd_playing">snd_Playing</h3>
<p>Returns 0 if sound has finished playing, else return number of 512 byte blocks to go.</p>
<p>This function is for control of a wav buffer, see the <a href="#file_playwav">file_PlayWAV(..)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_Playing();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Number of 512 byte blocks to go.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-176-1" name="__codelineno-176-1" href="#__codelineno-176-1"></a><span class="nl">count</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">snd_Playing</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// return number of sound blocks remaining</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="spi-control-functions">SPI Control Functions</h2>
<p>The SPI functions in this section apply to any general purpose SPI device.</p>
<h3 id="spi_init">spi_Init</h3>
<p>Sets up the PICASO SPI port to communicate with SPI devices. See the example in section <a href="#spi_read">spi_Read()</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Init(speed, input_mode, output_mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">speed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the speed of the SPI port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">input_mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the input mode of the SPI port. See diagram below.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">output_mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the output mode of the SPI port. See diagram below.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-177-1" name="__codelineno-177-1" href="#__codelineno-177-1"></a><span class="n">spi_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI_FAST</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                       </span><span class="c1">// init SPI at maximum speed for 16MB Flash</span>
<a id="__codelineno-177-2" name="__codelineno-177-2" href="#__codelineno-177-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-177-3" name="__codelineno-177-3" href="#__codelineno-177-3"></a><span class="n">spi_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI_SLOW</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">SPI_ADDRESS_MODE4</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="c1">// init SPI at Slow speed for 32MB</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The SPI functions in this section are not necessary when using the memory card or serial flash chips interfaced

<h3 id="spi_disable">spi_Disable</h3>
<p>This function raises the Chip Select (SDCS) line of the SPI device, disabling it from further activity. The CS line will be automatically lowered next time the SPI functions <a href="#spi_read">spi_Read()</a> or <a href="#spi_write">spi_Write(...)</a> are used, and also by the action of any <a href="#media-functions">media_functions</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Disable();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>

<td style="text-align: left;">Address of byte array or string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 id="str_match">str_Match</h3>
<p>Case Sensitive match.
Compares the string at position ptr in a string buffer to the string str, skipping over any leading spaces
if required. If a match occurs, ptr is advanced to the first position past the match, else ptr is not
altered.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Match(&amp;ptr, *str);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Address of byte pointer to string buffer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer string to match.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  0 if no match, else advance ptr to the next position after the match and returns a pointer to the match position.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="str_matchi">str_MatchI</h3>
<p>Case Insensitive match.
Compares the string at position ptr in a string buffer to the string str, skipping over any leading spaces
if required. If a match occurs, ptr is advanced to the first position past the match, else ptr is not altered.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_MatchI(&amp;ptr, *str);</code></p>

</thead>

<td style="text-align: left;">Address of the byte pointer to string buffer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer string to match.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  0 if no match, else advance ptr to the next position after the match and returns a pointer to the match position.</p>

<h3 id="str_find">str_Find</h3>
<p>Case Sensitive.
Given the address of a pointer to a source string as the first argument, and a pointer to a test string as the second argument, attempts to find the position of the matching string in the source string. The test is performed with case sensitivity.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Find(&amp;ptr, *str);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Byte pointer to string buffer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">String to find.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  0 if not found. Returns the address of the first character of the match if successful.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="str_findi">str_FindI</h3>
<p>Case Insensitive.
Given the address of a pointer to a source string as the first argument, and a pointer to a test string as the second argument, attempts to find the position of the matching string in the source string. The test is performed with case insensitivity, e.g. upper and lower case chars are accepted.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_FindI(&amp;ptr, *str);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Byte pointer to string buffer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">String to find.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  0 if not found. Returns the address of the first character of the match if successful.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-191-1" name="__codelineno-191-1" href="#__codelineno-191-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">buffer</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// 200 character buffer for a source string</span>

<h3 id="str_printf">str_Printf</h3>
<p>This function prints a formatted string from elements derived from a structured byte region. There is only one input argument, the byte region pointer ptr which is automatically advanced as the format specifier string is processed. The format string is similar to the C language, however, there are a few differences, including the addition of the indirection token * (asterix).</p>
<p id="format-specifiers"><b>Format Specifiers:</b></p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">format</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%c</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">character</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%s</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">string of characters</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%d</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">signed decimal</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%ld</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">long decimal</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%u</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">unsigned decimal</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%lu</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">long unsigned decimal</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%x</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">hex byte</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%X</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">hex word</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%lX</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">hex long</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%b</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">binary word</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%lb</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">long binary word</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>(*) indirection prefix (placed after '%' to specify indirect addressing)</p>
<p>(number) width description (use between '%' and format specifier to set the field width).</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Printf(&amp;ptr, *format);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Byte pointer to the input data (structure).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">format</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Format string. Check the <a href="#format-specifiers">format specifiers</a> above.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The position of last extraction point. This is useful for processing by other string functions.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-193-1" name="__codelineno-193-1" href="#__codelineno-193-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">buffer</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w">        </span><span class="c1">// 200 character buffer for a source string</span>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>The address of the pointer must be passed so the function can advance it as required.</li>
<li>The format specifier string can be a string pointer, allowing dynamic construction of the printing format.</li>
<li>If (number) is preceded by 0, the result is Left-pads with zeroes (0) instead of spaces.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="str_cat">str_Cat</h3>
<p>Appends a copy of the source string to the destination string. The terminating null character in destination is overwritten by the first character of source, and a new null-character is appended at the end of the new string formed by the concatenation of both in destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Cat(&amp;destination, &amp;source);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">destination</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination string address.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">source</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Source string address.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Pointer to the destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-194-1" name="__codelineno-194-1" href="#__codelineno-194-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w">               </span><span class="c1">// 200 character buffer for a source string</span>

<a id="__codelineno-194-3" name="__codelineno-194-3" href="#__codelineno-194-3"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>

<a id="__codelineno-194-10" name="__codelineno-194-10" href="#__codelineno-194-10"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">repeat</span>

<a id="__codelineno-194-12" name="__codelineno-194-12" href="#__codelineno-194-12"></a><span class="n">endfunc</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="str_catn">str_CatN</h3>
<p>The number of characters copied is limited by "count".
The terminating null character in destination is overwritten by the first character of source, and a new null-character 
is appended at the end of the new string formed by the concatenation of both in destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_CatN(&amp;ptr, str, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination string address.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Source string address.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of characters to be concatenated.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Pointer to the destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="str_bytemove">str_ByteMove</h3>
<p>Copy bytes from "src" to "dest", stopping only when "count" is exhausted. No terminator is appended, it is purely a 
byte copy, and any zeroes encountered will also be copied.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_ByteMove(src, dest, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">src</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned source.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of bytes to transfer.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the end of the destination (which is "dest" + "count").</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-196-1" name="__codelineno-196-1" href="#__codelineno-196-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">src</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">dest</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mybuf1</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mybuf2</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="c1">// string pointers and two 20 byte buffers</span>
<a id="__codelineno-196-2" name="__codelineno-196-2" href="#__codelineno-196-2"></a><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf1</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"TESTING 123"</span><span class="p">);</span>

<a id="__codelineno-196-5" name="__codelineno-196-5" href="#__codelineno-196-5"></a><span class="nl">dest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str_Ptr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf2</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-196-6" name="__codelineno-196-6" href="#__codelineno-196-6"></a><span class="n">src</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">+=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">                                   </span><span class="c1">// move src pointer to "G 123"</span>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="str_copy">str_Copy</h3>
<p>Copy a string from "src" to "dest", stopping only when the end of source string "src" is encountered (0x00 terminator). 
The terminator is always appended, even if "src" is an empty string.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Copy(dest, src);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">src</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned source.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the 0x00 string terminator at the end of "dest" (which is "dest" + str_Length(src); ).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-197-1" name="__codelineno-197-1" href="#__codelineno-197-1"></a><span class="nl">nextplace</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str_Copy</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">d</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="str_copyn">str_CopyN</h3>
<p>Copy a string from "src" to "dest", stopping only when "count" is exhausted, or end of source string "str" is 
encountered (0x00 string terminator). The terminator is always appended, even if "count" is zero, or "src" is a null string.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_CopyN(dest, src, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">src</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned source.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Maximum number of bytes to copy.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the 0x00 string terminator at the end of "dest" (which is "dest" + str_Length(src); ).</p>

<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-198-1" name="__codelineno-198-1" href="#__codelineno-198-1"></a><span class="nl">nextplace</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str_CopyN</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">d</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h2 id="system-memory-functions">System Memory Functions</h2>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>peekW(address);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

</code></pre></div>

<h2 id="text-and-string-functions">Text and String Functions</h2>
<h3 id="txt_movecursor">txt_MoveCursor</h3>
<p>Moves the text cursor to a screen position set by line and column parameters. The line and column position is calculated, based on the size and scaling factor for the currently selected font. When text is outputted to screen it will be displayed from this position. The text position could also be set with <a href="#gfx_moveto">gfx_MoveTo(...)</a>; if required to set the text position to an exact pixel location. Note that lines and columns start from 0, so line 0, column 0 is the top left corner of the display.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>txt_MoveCursor(line, column);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">line</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Holds a positive value for the required line position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">column</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Holds a positive value for the required column position.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-201-1" name="__codelineno-201-1" href="#__codelineno-201-1"></a><span class="n">txt_MoveCursor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">9</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-201-2" name="__codelineno-201-2" href="#__codelineno-201-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-201-3" name="__codelineno-201-3" href="#__codelineno-201-3"></a><span class="c1">// This example moves the text origin to the 5th line and the 10th column.</span>
</code></pre></div>

<p><strong>putch</strong> prints single characters to the current output stream, usually the display.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>putch(char);</code></p>

<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-202-1" name="__codelineno-202-1" href="#__codelineno-202-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">v</span><span class="p">;</span>

<a id="__codelineno-202-3" name="__codelineno-202-3" href="#__codelineno-202-3"></a><span class="n">putch</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">v</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="c1">// print the number 9 to the current display location</span>
<a id="__codelineno-202-4" name="__codelineno-202-4" href="#__codelineno-202-4"></a><span class="n">putch</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sc">'\n'</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">        </span><span class="c1">// newline</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="putstr">putstr</h3>
<p><strong>putstr</strong> prints a string to the current output stream, usually the display.
The argument can be a string constant, a pointer to a string, a pointer to an array, or a pointer to a data statement.</p>
<p>A string constant is automatically terminated with a zero.</p>
<p>A string in a data statement is not automatically terminated with a zero.</p>
<p>All variables in 4DGL are 16bit, if an array is used for holding 8-bit characters; each array element packs 1 or 2 characters.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>putstr(pointer);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">string</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A string constant or pointer to a string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The pointer to the item that was printed.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<div class="tabbed-content">
<div class="tabbed-block">
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-203-1" name="__codelineno-203-1" href="#__codelineno-203-1"></a><span class="c1">// Example #1print a string constant</span>
<a id="__codelineno-203-2" name="__codelineno-203-2" href="#__codelineno-203-2"></a><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"HELLO</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//simply print a string constant at current origin</span>
</code></pre></div>
</div>
<div class="tabbed-block">
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-204-1" name="__codelineno-204-1" href="#__codelineno-204-1"></a><span class="c1">// Example #2 print string via pointer</span>
<a id="__codelineno-204-2" name="__codelineno-204-2" href="#__codelineno-204-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// a var for use as a pointer</span>

<a id="__codelineno-204-4" name="__codelineno-204-4" href="#__codelineno-204-4"></a><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// print the string using the pointer</span>
<a id="__codelineno-204-5" name="__codelineno-204-5" href="#__codelineno-204-5"></a><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">p</span><span class="o">+</span><span class="mi">8</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// print, offsetting into the string</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="putnum">putnum</h3>

<a id="__codelineno-206-2" name="__codelineno-206-2" href="#__codelineno-206-2"></a><span class="nl">v</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mo">0567</span><span class="mi">8</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-206-3" name="__codelineno-206-3" href="#__codelineno-206-3"></a><span class="n">putnum</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">HEX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">v</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">             </span><span class="c1">// print the number as hex 4 digits</span>
<a id="__codelineno-206-4" name="__codelineno-206-4" href="#__codelineno-206-4"></a><span class="n">putnum</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BIN</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">v</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">             </span><span class="c1">// print the number as binary 16 digits</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="print">print</h3>
<p><strong>4DGL</strong> has a versatile <code>print(...)</code> statement for formatting numbers and strings. 
In its simplest form, print will simply print a number as can be seen below:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-207-1" name="__codelineno-207-1" href="#__codelineno-207-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-207-2" name="__codelineno-207-2" href="#__codelineno-207-2"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-207-3" name="__codelineno-207-3" href="#__codelineno-207-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-207-4" name="__codelineno-207-4" href="#__codelineno-207-4"></a><span class="c1">// This will print **100** to the current output device (usually the display in TEXT mode). </span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If you wish to add a string anywhere within a <code>print(...)</code> statement, just place a quoted string expression and you will be able to mix strings and numbers in a variety of formats. See the following example.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-208-1" name="__codelineno-208-1" href="#__codelineno-208-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"the value of myvar is :- "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"and its 8bit binary representation is:-"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">BIN8</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
</div>
<p>(*) Refer the table in <a href="#putnum">putnum(..)</a> for all the numeric representations available.</p>
<p>The <code>print(...)</code> statement will accept directives passed in square brackets to make it print in various ways, 
for instance, if you wish to print a number in 4 digit hex, use the <strong>[HEX4]</strong> directive placed in front 
of the variable to be displayed within the print statement. See the following example.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-209-1" name="__codelineno-209-1" href="#__codelineno-209-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"myvar as a 4 digit HEX number is :- "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">HEX4</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>There are 2 print directives that are not part of the numeric set and will be explained separately. 
These are the <strong>[STR]</strong> and <strong>[CHR]</strong> directives.</p>
</div>
<p>The <strong>[STR]</strong> directive expects a string pointer to follow:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-210-1" name="__codelineno-210-1" href="#__codelineno-210-1"></a><span class="nl">s</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"Hello World"</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// assign a string constant to s </span>
<a id="__codelineno-210-2" name="__codelineno-210-2" href="#__codelineno-210-2"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Var 's' points to a string constant at address"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">" which is"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">STR</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>The <strong>[CHR]</strong> directive prints the character value of a variable.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-211-1" name="__codelineno-211-1" href="#__codelineno-211-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"The third character of the string is '"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">CHR</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">s</span><span class="o">+</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">));</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>also</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-212-1" name="__codelineno-212-1" href="#__codelineno-212-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"The value of 'myvar' as an ASCII charater is '"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">CHR</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>You can freely mix string pointers, strings, variables and expressions within a print statement.
<code>print(...)</code> can also use the <a href="#to">to(...)</a> function to redirect it's output to a different output device 
other than the screen using the function (refer to the <a href="#to">to(...)</a> statement for further examples).</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>print(...);</code>    </p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-213-1" name="__codelineno-213-1" href="#__codelineno-213-1"></a><span class="cp">#platform "uOLED-32028-P1_GFX2"</span>
<a id="__codelineno-213-2" name="__codelineno-213-2" href="#__codelineno-213-2"></a><span class="c1">/////////////////////</span>

<h3 id="to">to</h3>
<p><strong>to()</strong> sends the printed output to destinations other than the screen. Normally, print just sends its output to the display in <strong>TEXT</strong> mode which is the default, however, the output from print can be sent to 'streams', e.g. – <strong>COM0</strong> or <strong>COM1</strong>, an open FAT16 file with <strong>DSK</strong>, to raw media with <strong>MDA</strong> (media), or to the I2C ports with <strong>I2C</strong>.</p>
<p>The <strong>to(...)</strong> function can also stream to a memory array . Note that once the <strong>to(...)</strong> function has taken effect, the stream reverts back to the default stream which is <strong>TEXT</strong> as soon as <a href="#putch">putch</a>, <a href="#putstr">putstr</a>, <a href="#putnum">putnum</a>, <a href="#print">print</a>, or <a href="#str_printf">str_Printf</a> has completed its action.</p>
<p>The <strong>APPEND</strong> argument is used to append the printed output to the same place as the previous redirection. 
This is most useful for building string arrays, or adding sequential data to a media stream.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Predefined Name</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Constant</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">putch, putstr, putnum, print, str_Printf redirection</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">APPEND</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0x0000</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is appended to user array if previous redirection was to an array.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">TEXT</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF801</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the <strong>screen</strong> (default).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">DSK</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF802</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the most recently open file that has been opened in write mode.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">COM0</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF804</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirected to the <strong>COM0</strong> (default serial) port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">COM1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xFF05</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirected to the <strong>COM1</strong> (auxiliary serial) port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF820</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the <strong>I2C</strong> port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">MDA</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF840</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the <strong>SD/SDHC</strong> or <strong>FLASH</strong> media.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">(memory pointer)</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Array Address</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirect to the <strong>memory</strong> pointer argument.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<div class="admonition warning">
<p class="admonition-title">Warning</p>
<p>Becareful writing to a FAT16 formatted card without checking legal partitioned else the disk formatting will be destroyed.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>to(outstream);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">outstream</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A variable or constant specifying the destination for the <a href="#putch">putch</a>, <a href="#putstr">putstr</a>, <a href="#putnum">putnum</a>, <a href="#print">print</a> and <a href="#str_printf">str_Printf</a> functions.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>

<h3 id="charwidth">charwidth</h3>
<p><strong>charwidth</strong> is used to calculate the width in pixel units for a string, based on the currently selected font.
The font can be proportional or monospaced. If the total width of the string exceeds 255 pixel
units, the function will return the 'wrapped' (modulo 8) value.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>charwidth('char');</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The ascii character for the width calculation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The width of a single character in pixel units.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-215-1" name="__codelineno-215-1" href="#__codelineno-215-1"></a><span class="c1">// Example</span>
<a id="__codelineno-215-2" name="__codelineno-215-2" href="#__codelineno-215-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-215-3" name="__codelineno-215-3" href="#__codelineno-215-3"></a><span class="nl">str</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"HELLO</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">THERE"</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">          </span><span class="c1">// note that this string spans 2 lines due to the \n.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-215-4" name="__codelineno-215-4" href="#__codelineno-215-4"></a><span class="nl">width</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">strwidth</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">str</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// get the width of the string, this will also capture the height.</span>

<h3 id="charheight">charheight</h3>
<p><strong>charheight</strong> is used to calculate the height in pixel units for a string, based on the currently selected font.
The font can be proportional or monospaced.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>charheight('char');</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The ascii character for the height calculation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The height of a single character in pixel units.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth()</a>.</p>
<h3 id="strwidth">strwidth</h3>
<p><strong>strwidth</strong> returns the width of a zero terminated string in pixel units. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strwidth(pointer);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pointer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The pointer to a zero (0x00) terminated string. 'pointer' may be a constant or pointer to word aligned variable.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The width of a string in pixel units, can be multiline.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth()</a>.</p>
<h3 id="strheight">strheight</h3>
<p><strong>strheight</strong> returns the height of a zero terminated string in pixel units. The <a href="#strwidth">strwidth</a> function must be called first which makes available width and height. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strheight();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The height of a string in pixel units, can be multiline.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth()</a>.</p>
<h3 id="strlen">strlen</h3>
<p><strong>strlen</strong> returns the length of a zero terminated string in character units. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strlen(pointer);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pointer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The pointer to a zero (0x00) terminated string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The length of a string in character units.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth()</a>.</p>
<h3 id="txt_set">txt_Set</h3>
<p>Given a function number and a value, set the required text control parameter, such as size, colour, and other formatting controls. This function is extremely useful in a loop to select multiple parameters from a data statement or a control array. Note also that each function available for <code>txt_Set</code> has a <a href="#single_parameter_shortcuts">single parameter 'shortcut' function</a> that has the same effect.</p>

<h2 id="timer-functions">Timer Functions</h2>
<h3 id="sys_t">sys_T</h3>
<p>Returns the current value of the rolling 32bit system timer (1mse) LO word.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_T();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value of system timer. (LO Word)</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-216-1" name="__codelineno-216-1" href="#__codelineno-216-1"></a><span class="nl">t</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">sys_T</span><span class="p">();</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sys_t_hi">sys_T_HI</h3>
<p>Returns the current value of the rolling 32bit system timer (1mse) HI word.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_T_HI();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value of system timer. (HI Word)</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="sys_settimer">sys_SetTimer</h3>

<h3 id="sys_settimerevent">sys_SetTimerEvent</h3>
<p>Set a function to be called for selected timer. When the timer reaches zero, the function is called. The called function must not have any parameters, and should not have a return value. This is necessary because the timer event is invoked asynchronously to the mainline program (i.e, it is not called in the normal way, so parameters and return values don’t apply).</p>
<p><a href="#sys_settimerevent">sys_SetTimerEvent(timernum, 0)</a> disables the timer event.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>When a child process is run using the file_run or file_exec function, or if a file was loaded with
file_Loadfunction and is executed, the loaded process gets its own code and memory space,
therefore, any timer that reaches zero that has a timer event attached in the parent code space, will
fail and cause a crash as an attempt is made to force the program counter to some wild place in the
child process - There are 2 ways to overcome this problem.</p>
<ol>
<li>If a child process will not be requiring the use of any timers or timer events, the parent program
can simply use the <a href="#sys_eventspostpone">eventsPostpone()</a> function before calling or entering the child process. Once the
parent program regains control, the <a href="#sys_eventsresume">eventsResume()</a> function will allow any events in the queue to
then be processed. The side effect of this method is that several events may bank up, and will execute
immediately once the <a href="#sys_eventsresume">eventsResume()</a> takes place. This however disallows a child process to use any
timer events in the sub program so method 2 is preferable in this case.</li>
<li>The parent program can 'disconnect' the event(s) by setting it/them to zero prior to child process execution, or setting the associated timer to zero so the event wont fire. In either case, it is necessary to do the following:</li>
</ol>
<p><code>while(sys_EventQueue());</code></p>
<p>to ensure the event queue is empty prior to calling the child process. Note also that if just the timer is set to zero, the child process cannot use this timer. If the timer was now set to a value and the old event still existed, when the timer reaches zero the 'bad' parent address event will fire causing a crash.</p>
<p>The reverse situation also applies of course, the same level of respect is required if a child program
needs to use any timer events. Method [1] (above) will not work as the events have been
postponed, stopping the child process from using any timer events. If the child process did an
<a href="#sys_eventsresume">eventsResume()</a> in this case, everything would crash miserably. So the same applies, a child that
uses any timer events must respect any timers that may be used by the parent, and a child must
zero the <strong>sys_SetTimerEvent</strong> before returning to the parent.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_SetTimerEvent(timernum, function);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">timernum</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">One of eight timers TIMER0 to TIMER7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">function</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Event Function to be queued.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Any previous event function address, or zero if there was no previous function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-220-1" name="__codelineno-220-1" href="#__codelineno-220-1"></a><span class="n">sys_SetTimerEvent</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">TIMER5</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myfunc</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sys_eventqueue">sys_EventQueue</h3>
<p>Returns the max number of events that were pending in the event queue since the last call to this function. 
This can be used to assess event overhead burden, especially after or during a <a href="#sys_eventspostpone">sys_EventsPostpone</a> action.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_EventQueue();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Number of events.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-221-1" name="__codelineno-221-1" href="#__codelineno-221-1"></a><span class="nl">tasks</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">sys_EventQueue</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sys_eventspostpone">sys_EventsPostpone</h3>
<p>Postpone any events until the <a href="#sys_eventsresume">sys_EventResume</a> function is executed. The event queue will continue to queue events, but no action will take place until a <a href="#sys_eventsresume">sys_EventResume</a> function is encountered.
The queue will continue to receive up to 32 events before discarding any further events. This function is required to allow a sequence of instructions or functions to occur that would otherwise be corrupted by an event occurring during the sequence of instructions or functions. A good example of this is when you set a position to print, if there was no way of locking the current sequence, an event may occur which does a similar thing, and a contention would occur - printing to the wrong position. This function should be used wisely, if any action that is required would take considerable time, it is better to disable any conflicting event functions with a bypass flag, then restart the conflicting event by re-issuing a timer value.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_EventsPostpone();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-222-1" name="__codelineno-222-1" href="#__codelineno-222-1"></a><span class="n">sys_EventsPostpone</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// postpone the event queue</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sys_eventsresume">sys_EventsResume</h3>
<p>Resume any postponed events. The queue will try to execute any events that were incurred during the postponed period. 
Note that queued events are only checked for and executed at the end of each 4DGL instruction.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_EventsResume();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-223-1" name="__codelineno-223-1" href="#__codelineno-223-1"></a><span class="n">sys_EventsResume</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// resume the event queue</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sys_deepsleep">sys_DeepSleep</h3>
<p>Deep Sleep is a sleep state that is ‘deeper’ than the regular Sleep (for most display modules) and therefore consumes less power. Some displays do not support being powered to a lower state, so sleep and deepsleep power consumption can sometimes be roughly the same.</p>
<p>Puts the display and processor into the lowest power mode for a period of time. If "units" is zero, the display goes into sleep mode forever and needs power cycling to re-initialize. If "units" is 1 to 65535, the display will sleep for that period of time, or will be woken when touch screen is touched. The function returns the count of "units" that are remaining when the screen was touched. When returning from deep sleep mode, some displays might lose their screen and/or need to be reinitialised with <a href="#disp_init">disp_Init()</a>.</p>
<p><em>New in v0.7 PmmC.</em></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_DeepSleep(units);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">units</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sleep timer units are approx 1 second. When in sleep mode, timing is controlled by an RC oscillator, therefore, timing is not totally accurate and should not be relied on for timing purposes.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Remaining time units when touch screen is touched, else returns zero.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-224-1" name="__codelineno-224-1" href="#__codelineno-224-1"></a><span class="n">sys_DeepSleep</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">60</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Sleep for 1 minute</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sys_sleep">sys_Sleep</h3>
<p>Regular sleep, which puts the display and processor into low power mode for a period of time. If "units" is zero, the display goes into sleep mode forever and needs power cycling to re-initialize. If "units" is 1 to 65535, the display will sleep for that period of time, or will be woken when touch screen is touched. The function returns the count of "units" that are remaining when the screen was touched. When returning from sleep mode, the display and processor are restored from low power mode.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p><a href="#sys_sleep">sys_Sleep()</a> was found to have an issue in PmmC’s prior to R33, the units value was not always near 1 second. This has been corrected in PmmC R33.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_Sleep(units);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">units</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sleep timer units are approx 1 second. When in sleep mode, timing is controlled by an RC oscillator, therefore, timing is not totally accurate and should not be relied on for timing purposes.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Remaining time units when touch screen is touched, else returns zero.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-225-1" name="__codelineno-225-1" href="#__codelineno-225-1"></a><span class="n">sys_Sleep</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">60</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Sleep for 1 minute</span>
</code></pre></div>

Y_RES is replaced with Y_MAX in the <a href="#gfx_clipwindow">gfx_ClipWindow()</a> function. <br> 6 - str_Append is replaced with str_Cat in the example in the <a href="#str_cat">str_Cat()</a> function. <br> 7 - str_Append is replaced with str_CatN in the example in the <a href="#str_catn">str_CatN()</a> function.</td>

Note SPI diagram in the <a href="#spi_init">spi_Init()</a> function. <br> 6 - Fixed typing error in the <a href="#sys_t">sys_T()</a> and <a href="#sys_t_hi">sys_T_HI()</a> functions. It's a 32 bit Timer. <br> 7 - Fixed typing error in the Description in the <a href="#i2c_open">I2C_Open()</a> function.</td>

If frame is set to -1, just a rectangle will be drawn in background colour to blank an image. It applies to PmmC R29 or above. See the <a href="#img_setword">img_SetWord()</a> function. <br> 8 - Description updated, Image control will now show error box for out of range video frames. Also, if frame is set to -1, just a rectangle will be drawn in background colour to blank an image. It applies to PmmC R29 or above. See the <a href="#media_videoframe">media_VideoFrame()</a> function.</td>
